-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- 5. The star schema (milestone 4).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,

  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,

CREATE TABLE dim_time (

  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),

);

  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL
  -- TODO: enforce the grain
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run the pipeline once for every batch in the landing zone, oldest first.

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landing_packet
ORDER BY batch_id;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('staged', '1', 1382), ('staged', '2', 1322), ('staged', '3', 2706),
  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('quarantine', '1:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '1:malformed_json',    2),
  ('quarantine', '1:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '1:non_numeric_value', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_satellite', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_sensor',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:malformed_json',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '2:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '3:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:unknown_sensor',    1);

CREATE VIEW test_quarantine AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'quarantine') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT batch_id || ':' || reason AS item, packets AS actual
                 FROM v_quarantine_summary) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

-- TODO (milestone 4): the hand counts and the view test_star.
CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT NULL AS test, NULL AS item, NULL AS expected, NULL AS actual
WHERE 1;

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
);
--- solution
-- =====================================================================
--  ORBIT fleet telemetry warehouse
--
--  One script builds the whole database from an empty file that holds
--  only the landing zone (landing_packet). The layers, in the order the
--  data flows through them:
--
--    1. operational schema   the fleet, as the operations team keeps it
--    2. pipeline control     runs and steps, one trigger per step
--    3. staging              every landed packet, parsed, not trusted
--    4. quarantine           rejected packets, each with one reason
--    5. star schema          dimensions and the fact table
--    6. rollups              hourly and daily aggregates
--    7. trend reports        window functions over the facts
--    8. gaps and islands     outages, empty hours, low-battery streaks
--    9. data quality         checks that must return zero rows
--   10. report suite         what operations reads every morning
--
--  Conventions: times are UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; every step can
--  be rerun for the same batch without changing the result.
-- =====================================================================

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Operational schema: the fleet as the operations team keeps it.
--    Normalised: each fact about the fleet is stored exactly once, and
--    the constraints refuse any row that could not be true.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE satellite (
  sat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (code GLOB 'ORB-[0-9]*'),
  name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  launched_on  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (launched_on IS date(launched_on)),
  status       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                       CHECK (status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  status_since TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status_since >= launched_on)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor_type (
  type_code  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CHECK (type_code = lower(type_code)),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT NOT NULL,
  min_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  max_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  CHECK (min_valid < max_valid)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor (
  sensor_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES sensor_type (type_code),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE ground_station (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (length(code) = 3 AND code = upper(code)),
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  latitude   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90),
  longitude  REAL NOT NULL CHECK (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180)
);

-- A planned contact: the satellite is above the station's horizon from
-- aos (acquisition of signal) until los (loss of signal).
CREATE TABLE contact_pass (
  pass_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_station (station_id),
  aos        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (aos IS datetime(aos, '+0 seconds')),
  los        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (los IS datetime(los, '+0 seconds')),
  CHECK (los > aos),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, aos)
);

-- channel, so 23 is ORB-2's flight computer thermometer.

-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The star schema. Grain of the fact table: one reading of one
--    sensor at one moment. Dimensions use surrogate keys (sat_key,
--    sensor_key, time_key) so the warehouse does not depend on how the
--    operational tables number things.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: satellite.sat_id
  sat_code  TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: sensor.sensor_id
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,         -- copied in, so reports need no extra join
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_label TEXT    NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: ground_station.station_id
  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  station_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  hemisphere   TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (hemisphere IN ('N', 'S'))  -- derived from latitude
);

-- A calendar, one row per hour, with no holes: an hour with no readings
-- still has a row, which is how reports can show it as empty.
CREATE TABLE dim_time (
  time_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                               -- YYYYMMDDHH
  hour_start TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,                           -- '2026-03-01 14:00:00'
  day        TEXT    NOT NULL,                                  -- '2026-03-01'
  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),
  weekday    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Sunday
  shift      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (shift IN ('A', 'B', 'C'))  -- 00-08, 08-16, 16-24
);

CREATE TABLE fact_reading (
  reading_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  ts         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  value      REAL    NOT NULL,
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- lineage: the batch this version came from
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)       -- the grain, enforced
);

-- The clean rows of every batch, one per sensor and moment: when a batch
-- holds the same reading twice, its last line wins.
CREATE VIEW v_stg_accepted AS
SELECT r.batch_id,
       r.line_no,
       d.sensor_key,
       CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', r.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time_key,
       r.ts,
       r.value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         sensor_id,
         ts,
         value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
                            ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE reject_reason IS NULL
) r
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_load AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'load'
BEGIN
  -- Dimensions first: a fact may only point at rows that exist.
  INSERT INTO dim_satellite (sat_id, sat_code, sat_name, status)
  SELECT sat_id, code, name, status
  FROM satellite
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY sat_id
  ON CONFLICT (sat_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_code = excluded.sat_code,
    sat_name = excluded.sat_name,
    status   = excluded.status;

  INSERT INTO dim_sensor (sensor_id, sat_key, sat_code, type_code, type_label, unit)
  SELECT se.sensor_id, ds.sat_key, ds.sat_code, st.type_code, st.label, st.unit
  FROM sensor se
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = se.sat_id
  JOIN sensor_type   st ON st.type_code = se.type_code
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY se.sensor_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_key    = excluded.sat_key,
    sat_code   = excluded.sat_code,
    type_label = excluded.type_label,
    unit       = excluded.unit;

  INSERT INTO dim_station (station_id, station_code, station_name, hemisphere)
  SELECT station_id, code, name, CASE WHEN latitude >= 0 THEN 'N' ELSE 'S' END
  FROM ground_station
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY station_id
  ON CONFLICT (station_id) DO UPDATE SET
    station_code = excluded.station_code,
    station_name = excluded.station_name,
    hemisphere   = excluded.hemisphere;

  -- The calendar: every hour from the earliest to the latest known reading.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (time_key, hour_start, day, hour, weekday, shift)
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         h,
         date(h),
         CAST(strftime('%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         CAST(strftime('%w', h) AS INTEGER),
         CASE WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '08' THEN 'A'
              WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '16' THEN 'B'
              ELSE 'C' END
  FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (
      SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours
      WHERE h < (SELECT MAX(last_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MAX(hour_start) AS last_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MAX(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL))
    )
    SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL
  );

  -- Facts: new readings only; a reading already in the warehouse stays.
  INSERT INTO fact_reading (sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no)
  SELECT sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no
  FROM v_stg_accepted
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO NOTHING;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run the pipeline once for every batch in the landing zone, oldest first.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landing_packet
ORDER BY batch_id;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('staged', '1', 1382), ('staged', '2', 1322), ('staged', '3', 2706),
  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('quarantine', '1:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '1:malformed_json',    2),
  ('quarantine', '1:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '1:non_numeric_value', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_satellite', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_sensor',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:malformed_json',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '2:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '3:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:unknown_sensor',    1);

CREATE VIEW test_quarantine AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'quarantine') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT batch_id || ':' || reason AS item, packets AS actual
                 FROM v_quarantine_summary) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('facts', 'ORB-1', 1144), ('facts', 'ORB-2', 1137), ('facts', 'ORB-3', 1104),
  ('facts', 'ORB-4', 1148), ('facts', 'ORB-5', 846),
  ('dims', 'dim_satellite', 6), ('dims', 'dim_sensor', 23),
  ('dims', 'dim_station', 4),   ('dims', 'dim_time', 48);

CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test IN ('facts', 'dims')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'facts' AS test, d.sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading f
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_code
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_satellite', COUNT(*) FROM dim_satellite
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_sensor',    COUNT(*) FROM dim_sensor
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_station',   COUNT(*) FROM dim_station
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_time',      COUNT(*) FROM dim_time) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
);
--- hint
`v_stg_accepted` is a join of `dim_sensor` to a subquery over `stg_reading WHERE reject_reason IS NULL` that adds `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank`; keep `copy_rank = 1` in the outer `WHERE`.
--- hint
Each dimension upsert is `INSERT INTO … SELECT … FROM … WHERE true ORDER BY … ON CONFLICT (natural key) DO UPDATE SET col = excluded.col, …`. For the calendar, the first hour is `SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time UNION ALL SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)`, and the last hour is the same with `MAX`.
--- hint
Put the recursive CTE inside a subquery: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (…) SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER), h, date(h), … FROM (WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (SELECT <first hour> UNION ALL SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours WHERE h < <last hour>) SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL)`. The `IS NOT NULL` covers a batch with no clean rows on an empty calendar.
--- check query | Each run loaded its batch: clean rows in, facts out
SELECT batch_id, rows_in, rows_out FROM etl_step WHERE step = 'load' ORDER BY step_id
=> [[1, 1373, 1369], [2, 1319, 1308], [3, 2702, 2702]]
--- check query | 5,379 facts, and never two for one sensor and moment
SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT sensor_key || '/' || ts) FROM fact_reading

+++ practice | A calendar of days
--- schema
CREATE TABLE dim_day (
  day_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  day       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  weekday   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  is_weekend INTEGER NOT NULL
);
--- task
Fill the empty table `dim_day (day_key, day, weekday, is_weekend)` with one row for **every** day from `'2026-02-26'` to `'2026-03-04'`, inclusive:

- `day_key`: the date as a number `YYYYMMDD`, for example 20260226
- `day`: the date as `'YYYY-MM-DD'`
- `weekday`: 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday, from `strftime('%w', …)`, as an integer
- `is_weekend`: 1 on Saturday and Sunday, 0 otherwise

Use one `INSERT … SELECT` with a recursive CTE that counts the days.
--- starter
INSERT INTO dim_day (day_key, day, weekday, is_weekend)
SELECT 20260226, '2026-02-26', 4, 0;
--- solution
INSERT INTO dim_day (day_key, day, weekday, is_weekend)
WITH RECURSIVE days (d) AS (
  SELECT '2026-02-26'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(d, '+1 day') FROM days WHERE d < '2026-03-04'
)
SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d', d) AS INTEGER),
       d,
       CAST(strftime('%w', d) AS INTEGER),
       strftime('%w', d) IN ('0', '6')
FROM days;
--- hint
Start the CTE at the first day, and add a day with `date(d, '+1 day')` while `d` is before the last day. The last row produced is then the last day itself.
--- hint
`strftime('%Y%m%d', d)` and `strftime('%w', d)` give text: wrap them in `CAST(… AS INTEGER)`. `is_weekend` is the test `strftime('%w', d) IN ('0', '6')`, which gives 1 or 0.
--- check query | Seven days, first and last included, no gaps
SELECT COUNT(*), MIN(day), MAX(day) FROM dim_day
=> [[7, "2026-02-26", "2026-03-04"]]
--- check query | 28 February 2026 is a Saturday, 1 March a Sunday
SELECT day_key, weekday, is_weekend FROM dim_day WHERE day IN ('2026-02-28', '2026-03-01', '2026-03-02') ORDER BY day
=> [[20260228, 6, 1], [20260301, 0, 1], [20260302, 1, 0]]
--- check query | The keys and the weekdays are integers
SELECT typeof(day_key), typeof(weekday), SUM(is_weekend) FROM dim_day
=> [["integer", "integer", 2]]

+++ practice | Surrogate keys that stay put
--- schema
CREATE TABLE ops_tank (tank_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY, fluid TEXT NOT NULL, litres REAL NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO ops_tank VALUES ('T-OX', 'oxidiser', 820), ('T-FU', 'fuel', 640), ('T-HE', 'helium', 90);
CREATE TABLE dim_tank (
  tank_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  tank_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  fluid     TEXT NOT NULL,
  litres    REAL NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE sync_request (request_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
--- task
The operational table `ops_tank (tank_code, fluid, litres)` feeds the dimension `dim_tank (tank_key, tank_code, fluid, litres)`, whose `tank_key` is a surrogate key.

Create the trigger `sync_tanks`: after a row is inserted into `sync_request`, upsert every tank of `ops_tank` into `dim_tank`, **in order of `tank_code`**, so new tanks get the next keys; a tank already there keeps its key and has `fluid` and `litres` updated. Then insert one row into `sync_request`.
--- starter
CREATE TRIGGER sync_tanks AFTER INSERT ON sync_request
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM dim_tank;
  INSERT INTO dim_tank (tank_code, fluid, litres)
  SELECT tank_code, fluid, litres FROM ops_tank;
END;

INSERT INTO sync_request DEFAULT VALUES;
--- solution
CREATE TRIGGER sync_tanks AFTER INSERT ON sync_request
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO dim_tank (tank_code, fluid, litres)
  SELECT tank_code, fluid, litres
  FROM ops_tank
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY tank_code
  ON CONFLICT (tank_code) DO UPDATE SET
    fluid  = excluded.fluid,
    litres = excluded.litres;
END;

INSERT INTO sync_request DEFAULT VALUES;
--- hint
Deleting and re-inserting gives every tank a new key on every sync, which breaks every fact that points at the old keys. An upsert keeps the row, and so keeps its key.
--- hint
`INSERT INTO dim_tank (…) SELECT … FROM ops_tank WHERE true ORDER BY tank_code ON CONFLICT (tank_code) DO UPDATE SET fluid = excluded.fluid, litres = excluded.litres`. The `WHERE true` tells SQLite the `ON CONFLICT` is not part of a join.
--- check query | Keys in order of code
SELECT tank_key, tank_code FROM dim_tank ORDER BY tank_key
=> [[1, "T-FU"], [2, "T-HE"], [3, "T-OX"]]
--- check query | A resize is updated in place; a new tank gets key 4; no key moves
UPDATE ops_tank SET litres = 700 WHERE tank_code = 'T-FU';
INSERT INTO ops_tank VALUES ('T-AA', 'water', 40);
INSERT INTO sync_request DEFAULT VALUES;
SELECT tank_key, tank_code, litres FROM dim_tank ORDER BY tank_key
=> [[1, "T-FU", 700.0], [2, "T-HE", 90.0], [3, "T-OX", 820.0], [4, "T-AA", 40.0]]
--- check query | Syncing again changes nothing
INSERT INTO sync_request DEFAULT VALUES;
SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(tank_key) FROM dim_tank
=> [[4, 4]]

+++ practice | Loading facts through their keys
--- schema
CREATE TABLE dim_pump (pump_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pump_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
INSERT INTO dim_pump VALUES (1, 'P1'), (2, 'P2'), (3, 'P3');
CREATE TABLE stg_flow (
  batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pump_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  ts       TEXT NOT NULL,
  lpm      REAL NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO stg_flow VALUES
  (1, 1, 'P1', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 12.0),
  (1, 2, 'P2', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 9.5),
  (1, 3, 'P1', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 12.4),
  (1, 4, 'P3', '2026-03-01 10:05:00', 7.0),
  (1, 5, 'P2', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 9.5),
  (1, 6, 'P1', '2026-03-01 10:05:00', 11.8);
CREATE TABLE fact_flow (
  pump_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_pump (pump_key),
  ts       TEXT NOT NULL,
  lpm      REAL NOT NULL,
  line_no  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (pump_key, ts)
);
--- task
Flow readings are staged in `stg_flow (batch_id, line_no, pump_code, ts, lpm)`. The fact table is `fact_flow (pump_key, ts, lpm, line_no)`, with the grain one reading per pump per moment, and `dim_pump (pump_key, pump_code)` maps codes to keys.

Insert batch 1 into `fact_flow` with one `INSERT … SELECT`: turn each `pump_code` into its `pump_key`, and when the batch holds the same pump and moment more than once, keep only the line with the highest `line_no`.
--- starter
INSERT INTO fact_flow (pump_key, ts, lpm, line_no)
SELECT DISTINCT d.pump_key, s.ts, s.lpm, s.line_no
FROM stg_flow s
JOIN dim_pump d ON d.pump_code = s.pump_code
WHERE s.batch_id = 1;
--- solution
INSERT INTO fact_flow (pump_key, ts, lpm, line_no)
SELECT d.pump_key, r.ts, r.lpm, r.line_no
FROM (
  SELECT pump_code, ts, lpm, line_no,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pump_code, ts ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_flow
  WHERE batch_id = 1
) r
JOIN dim_pump d ON d.pump_code = r.pump_code
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;
--- hint
The starter stops on the unique constraint: `DISTINCT` compares whole rows, and two copies with different line numbers, or different values, are different rows.
--- hint
Number the copies of each (pump, moment) from the last line down with `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pump_code, ts ORDER BY line_no DESC)` in a subquery, then join to `dim_pump` and keep `copy_rank = 1`.
--- check query | Four facts, one per pump and moment
SELECT pump_key, ts, lpm, line_no FROM fact_flow ORDER BY pump_key, ts
=> [[1, "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 12.4, 3], [1, "2026-03-01 10:05:00", 11.8, 6], [2, "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 9.5, 5], [3, "2026-03-01 10:05:00", 7.0, 4]]
--- check query | P1 at 10:00 keeps its last line, 12.4
SELECT lpm, line_no FROM fact_flow WHERE pump_key = 1 AND ts = '2026-03-01 10:00:00'
=> [[12.4, 3]]
--- check query | P2's exact repeat collapses into one row
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_flow WHERE pump_key = 2
=> [[1]]

+++ practice | The report that counted every reading four times
--- schema
CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sat_code TEXT NOT NULL, type_code TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO dim_sensor VALUES (1, 'ORB-1', 'batt_v'), (2, 'ORB-1', 'cpu_t'), (3, 'ORB-2', 'batt_v'), (4, 'ORB-2', 'cpu_t');
CREATE TABLE fact_reading (sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO fact_reading VALUES
  (1, '2026-03-01 00:00:00', 28.0), (1, '2026-03-01 00:10:00', 28.2),
  (2, '2026-03-01 00:00:00', 31.0), (2, '2026-03-01 00:10:00', 31.5),
  (3, '2026-03-01 00:00:00', 27.8), (4, '2026-03-01 00:00:00', 30.0);
--- task
This view should give each satellite's number of readings and its average battery voltage. It says ORB-1 has 8 readings and ORB-2 has 4, when they have 4 and 2:

```sql
CREATE VIEW sat_summary AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       COUNT(*) AS readings,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN b.type_code = 'batt_v' THEN f.value END), 2) AS avg_batt_v
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
JOIN dim_sensor b ON b.sat_code = d.sat_code
GROUP BY d.sat_code;
```

Fix `sat_summary`, keeping its name and its three columns, so each reading is counted once and `avg_batt_v` averages only battery readings.
--- starter
CREATE VIEW sat_summary AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       COUNT(*) AS readings,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN b.type_code = 'batt_v' THEN f.value END), 2) AS avg_batt_v
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
JOIN dim_sensor b ON b.sat_code = d.sat_code
GROUP BY d.sat_code;
--- solution
CREATE VIEW sat_summary AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       COUNT(*) AS readings,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'batt_v' THEN f.value END), 2) AS avg_batt_v
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
GROUP BY d.sat_code;
--- hint
Each fact row joins to one sensor through its key. The second join, on `sat_code`, matches every sensor of that satellite, so each reading turns into two rows before it is counted.
--- hint
Drop the second join. The first one already tells you the reading's type: use `d.type_code` inside the `CASE`.
--- check query | Four and two readings
SELECT sat_code, readings, avg_batt_v FROM sat_summary ORDER BY sat_code
=> [["ORB-1", 4, 28.1], ["ORB-2", 2, 27.8]]
--- check query | The total matches the fact table
SELECT SUM(readings) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading) FROM sat_summary
=> [[1]]
--- check query | A new sensor on ORB-1 does not change its numbers
INSERT INTO dim_sensor VALUES (5, 'ORB-1', 'wheel_rpm');
SELECT readings, avg_batt_v FROM sat_summary WHERE sat_code = 'ORB-1'
=> [[4, 28.1]]

+++ practice | Two versions of one reading
--- schema
CREATE TABLE stg (

--- task
Staged readings arrive in `stg (batch_id, line_no, sensor_id, ts, value)`. Within one batch, the same sensor and moment may appear several times: exact repeats, or a changed value.

Create the view `accepted (batch_id, line_no, sensor_id, ts, value)` that keeps, for each batch, sensor and moment, only the line with the highest `line_no`. Two different batches never hide each other: batch 8's reading of sensor 11 at 10:00 stays next to batch 7's.
--- starter
CREATE VIEW accepted AS
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id, MAX(line_no) AS line_no, sensor_id, ts, value
FROM stg
GROUP BY sensor_id, ts;
--- solution
CREATE VIEW accepted AS
SELECT batch_id, line_no, sensor_id, ts, value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, sensor_id, ts, value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg
)
WHERE copy_rank = 1;
--- hint
Grouping by sensor and moment alone mixes the batches together, and pairing `MAX(line_no)` with a plain `value` column in a `GROUP BY` does not promise that the value comes from that line.
--- hint
Number the copies with `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts ORDER BY line_no DESC)` in a subquery, and keep number 1. The batch is part of the partition.
--- check query | Five accepted rows
SELECT batch_id, line_no, sensor_id, ts, value FROM accepted ORDER BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
=> [[7, 4, 11, "2026-03-02 10:00:00", 28.3], [7, 3, 12, "2026-03-02 10:00:00", 40.0], [7, 5, 12, "2026-03-02 10:10:00", 45.0], [8, 1, 11, "2026-03-02 10:00:00", 27.9], [8, 3, 13, "2026-03-02 10:00:00", 31.0]]
--- check query | Batch 7 changed its mind about sensor 11: the last value, 28.3, wins
SELECT value, line_no FROM accepted WHERE batch_id = 7 AND sensor_id = 11
=> [[28.3, 4]]
--- check query | Batch 8 still has its own reading of sensor 11
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accepted WHERE sensor_id = 11
=> [[2]]

+++ practice | A star for ground station downlinks
--- schema
CREATE TABLE downlink_log (
  station_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  sat_code     TEXT NOT NULL,
  started      TEXT NOT NULL,
  megabytes    REAL NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO downlink_log VALUES
  ('SVB', 'ORB-1', '2026-03-01 01:12:00', 310.5),
  ('SVB', 'ORB-2', '2026-03-01 02:03:00', 290.0),
  ('AWA', 'ORB-1', '2026-03-01 09:15:00', 305.0),
  ('AWA', 'ORB-3', '2026-03-01 11:44:00', 120.0),
  ('SVB', 'ORB-1', '2026-03-02 01:10:00', 330.0),
  ('PUN', 'ORB-2', '2026-03-02 03:05:00', 0.0);
--- task
The ground network logs one row per downlink in `downlink_log (station_code, sat_code, started, megabytes)`. Build a small star for it:

1. `dim_station (station_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)` and `dim_sat (sat_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sat_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)`, each filled from the log with keys given **in order of code**.
2. `fact_downlink (station_key, sat_key, day, started, megabytes)`, grain one downlink, with `station_key` and `sat_key` referencing the dimensions, `day` the date of `started`, and `UNIQUE (station_key, started)`. Fill it from the log.
3. The view `station_day (station_code, day, downlinks, megabytes)`: downlinks and megabytes per station and day, one row for each station and day that has downlinks.
--- starter
CREATE TABLE dim_station (station_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE dim_sat (sat_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sat_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
--- solution
CREATE TABLE dim_station (station_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE dim_sat (sat_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sat_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);

INSERT INTO dim_station (station_code)
SELECT DISTINCT station_code FROM downlink_log ORDER BY station_code;

INSERT INTO dim_sat (sat_code)
SELECT DISTINCT sat_code FROM downlink_log ORDER BY sat_code;

CREATE TABLE fact_downlink (
  station_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_station (station_key),
  sat_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sat (sat_key),
  day         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  started     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  megabytes   REAL    NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (station_key, started)
);

INSERT INTO fact_downlink (station_key, sat_key, day, started, megabytes)
SELECT st.station_key, sa.sat_key, date(l.started), l.started, l.megabytes
FROM downlink_log l
JOIN dim_station st ON st.station_code = l.station_code
JOIN dim_sat     sa ON sa.sat_code = l.sat_code;

CREATE VIEW station_day AS
SELECT st.station_code,
       f.day,
       COUNT(*) AS downlinks,
       SUM(f.megabytes) AS megabytes
FROM fact_downlink f
JOIN dim_station st ON st.station_key = f.station_key
GROUP BY st.station_code, f.day;
--- hint
Fill the dimensions first, with `SELECT DISTINCT … ORDER BY` code, leaving the key out so the `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` numbers the rows as they arrive.
--- hint
The fact insert joins the log to both dimensions on their codes to pick up the keys. The view joins the facts back to `dim_station` and groups by code and day.
--- check query | Keys in order of code
SELECT (SELECT group_concat(station_code, ',') FROM (SELECT station_code FROM dim_station ORDER BY station_key)), (SELECT group_concat(sat_code, ',') FROM (SELECT sat_code FROM dim_sat ORDER BY sat_key))
=> [["AWA,PUN,SVB", "ORB-1,ORB-2,ORB-3"]]
--- check query | Six facts, each pointing at real dimension rows
SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(station_key IN (SELECT station_key FROM dim_station) AND sat_key IN (SELECT sat_key FROM dim_sat)) FROM fact_downlink
=> [[6, 6]]
--- check query | station_day, in order
SELECT station_code, day, downlinks, megabytes FROM station_day ORDER BY station_code, day
=> [["AWA", "2026-03-01", 2, 425.0], ["PUN", "2026-03-02", 1, 0.0], ["SVB", "2026-03-01", 2, 600.5], ["SVB", "2026-03-02", 1, 330.0]]
--- check query | The grain is enforced
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_index_list('fact_downlink') WHERE "unique" = 1
=> [[1]]

=== cap-data-05 | Data system 5: incremental, idempotent loads
--- teach
Last milestone the load put each batch's readings into the fact table and kept the first version of any reading it had already seen. That rule is too simple. Batch 2 re-sends eight of batch 1's readings unchanged, and it carries one **correction**: ORB-1's battery at 10:50 on 1 March was 28.4 V in batch 1, and batch 2 says it was 28.35 V. The warehouse still says 28.4. This milestone decides which version wins, and makes the load safe to run again, and in any order.

### Three properties of a good load

- **Incremental:** each run processes one batch, not the whole history. Reloading everything every time is simple, but its cost grows with the history, and it rewrites rows that reports have already used.
- **Idempotent:** running a batch twice leaves the database as running it once. [[Operators retry|retry]], schedulers double-fire, and a crash halfway leaves no choice but to run again.
- **Order-independent:** loading batch 5 and then batch 4 ends in the same facts as 4 then 5. Batches really do arrive out of order: a ground station that was offline delivers yesterday's pass after today's.

The third is the strongest. It says the fact table is a function of the **set** of batches loaded, not of the history of runs.

### Which version wins

For one sensor and moment, several batches may bring a version. The candidates for a rule:

| rule | problem |
| --- | --- |
| first loaded wins | corrections are ignored forever |
| last loaded wins | rerunning an old batch undoes a correction; out-of-order arrival picks the wrong version |
| latest `received_at` wins | clocks on different stations disagree, and ties are common |
| **highest `batch_id` wins** | none: the ground system numbers batches in the order it sent them |

So: **the version from the batch with the highest `batch_id` wins**, whatever order the loads happen in. A later batch is newer information about the same moment.

This uses one fact from outside the database: batch numbers are given out in increasing order by one sender. When you choose a rule like this for a real system, write that assumption down, because the rule is only as good as it is.

### The upsert that implements it

`INSERT … ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` can carry its own `WHERE`, which decides whether the existing row is updated at all. In it, `excluded` is the row that tried to go in, and the table's name means the row already there:

```sql fragment
ON CONFLICT (item, moment) DO UPDATE SET
  amount = excluded.amount,
  seq    = excluded.seq
WHERE excluded.seq > stock.seq;
```

Here the key is `(sensor_key, ts)` and the version number is `batch_id`. A new reading is inserted. A reading from an older or equal batch is skipped. A reading from a newer batch replaces the value and the lineage, `batch_id` and `line_no`.

Note what happens to an exact re-send in a later batch: the value does not change, but the lineage moves to the later batch. That looks like wasted work, and it is what makes the rule depend on nothing but batch numbers. If equal values kept the older lineage, the lineage would depend on which batch was loaded first.

### Why it is correct

Take one key, and call v(b) the version batch b brings for it. The claim: after any sequence of loads, the fact row holds the version from the highest-numbered batch loaded so far that has this key.

- **Before any load** there is no row, and no batch has been loaded. True.
- **Loading batch b.** If there is no row yet, b's version is inserted, and b is the only batch with this key so far. If there is a row from batch c, the `WHERE` updates it exactly when b > c. So afterwards it holds the version of max(b, c), and c was the maximum before. True again.

The maximum of a set does not depend on the order its elements arrive in, and taking the maximum twice changes nothing. So the load is both [[order-independent and idempotent|commutative]].

### Recording corrections

A correction changes a number someone may already have read in a report. Operations wants a record: which reading, the old and new value, the two batches, and the run that did it. So before the upsert, the load inserts into `fact_correction` every reading where the incoming batch is newer **and** the value differs:

```sql fragment
FROM incoming a
JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = a.sensor_key AND f.ts = a.ts
WHERE a.batch_id > f.batch_id AND a.value <> f.value
```

It must run before the upsert: afterwards the old value is gone. Unlike the facts, this log *does* depend on the order of the loads. Load 5 before 4 and batch 4's older version never gets in, so there is nothing to correct. That is fine: the log is a record of what happened, and the facts are the truth.

### Which batches have been loaded

`etl_batch` has one row per loaded batch: its first run, its last run, and how many times it has run. A [[high-water mark|watermark]], "the highest batch loaded so far, load anything above it", is the usual shortcut. Here it is rejected, because a late batch below the mark would never be loaded. A set of loaded batches answers "has batch 4 been loaded?" exactly, whatever the order.

`v_pipeline_monitor` turns the step log into one row per run: staged, clean, rejected, facts owned, corrections. Rejected is the validate step's rows in minus rows out.

### What it costs

The correction query and the upsert each look up every incoming reading in the `UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)` index: O(log F) per reading, O(n log F) for a batch of n. Nothing else in the warehouse is read or written, which is what "incremental" buys: the cost follows the size of the batch, not of the history.

### How to test it

After the three batches, batch 1 owns 1,360 facts (its 1,369 minus the nine that batch 2 re-sent or corrected), batch 2 owns 1,317 and batch 3 owns 2,702, and there is exactly one correction. The checks rerun old and new batches, and land two new batches that overlap, loading them in both orders and comparing the results.

**Watch out:** an upsert without the `WHERE` on its `DO UPDATE` works in every test that loads batches in order, once each. It is "last loaded wins": the first time someone reruns batch 1, it quietly puts 28.4 back and the correction is gone. And the correction log needs both halves of its condition, newer **and** different: with only "newer", every exact re-send is logged as a correction; with `>=` instead of `>`, every rerun is.

::: context retry Why systems run things twice
Real pipelines run on machines that crash, over networks that drop connections. A job that dies after doing half its work cannot know which half; the safe move is to run it again. Message systems promise delivery "at least once" for the same reason: they would rather deliver a batch twice than lose it. Idempotent steps turn "at least once" into "exactly once" in effect. That is why every step in this pipeline, from staging on, can be run twice without harm.
:::

::: context commutative Order that does not matter
An operation is commutative when the order of its inputs does not change the result: 3 + 5 = 5 + 3. Taking the larger of two numbers is commutative, and so is the load, because each key keeps the version from the larger batch number. Idempotent means that doing something twice is the same as doing it once: max(5, 5) = 5. Together they make the load robust against the two things networks do most: deliver late, and deliver twice.
:::

::: context watermark The high-water mark
A high-water mark is the highest level a flood has reached, painted on a wall. In data pipelines it is the largest batch number, or the latest timestamp, loaded so far: the next run loads everything above it. It is simple and cheap, and works when data always arrives in order. It fails when a late batch arrives below the mark, because the next run never looks there. Keeping the set of loaded batches costs one row per batch and has no blind spot.
:::
--- task
The load step already upserts the dimensions, fills the calendar and inserts the facts. Change it, and add what is missing:

1. Create the table `fact_correction` with the columns `correction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, `sensor_key` (required, referencing `dim_sensor`), `ts` (required), `old_value` and `new_value` (required numbers), `old_batch` (required), `new_batch` (required, and greater than `old_batch`) and `run_id` (required, referencing `etl_run`).
2. Create the table `etl_batch` with `batch_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, `first_run` and `last_run` (required, referencing `etl_run`) and `runs` (required, at least 1).
3. In `etl_load`, before the fact insert, insert into `fact_correction` one row for every accepted row of the batch whose key is already in `fact_reading` from an older batch with a different value (`run_id` is the step row's `run_id`).
4. Change the fact insert so that on a conflict on `(sensor_key, ts)` it updates `value`, `batch_id` and `line_no`, but only when the incoming `batch_id` is greater than the existing one.
5. After the facts, record the batch in `etl_batch`: a new batch gets `first_run` = `last_run` = this run and `runs` = 1; a batch seen before gets `last_run` = this run and `runs` one higher.
6. Replace the stub view `v_pipeline_monitor` with one row per run: `run_id`, `batch_id`, `staged` (the stage step's `rows_out`), `clean` (the validate step's `rows_out`), `rejected` (the validate step's `rows_in - rows_out`), `facts_owned` (the load step's `rows_out`) and `corrections` (rows of `fact_correction` with this `run_id`).

--- starter
-- =====================================================================
--  ORBIT fleet telemetry warehouse
--
--  One script builds the whole database from an empty file that holds
--  only the landing zone (landing_packet). The layers, in the order the
--  data flows through them:
--
--    1. operational schema   the fleet, as the operations team keeps it
--    2. pipeline control     runs and steps, one trigger per step
--    3. staging              every landed packet, parsed, not trusted
--    4. quarantine           rejected packets, each with one reason
--    5. star schema          dimensions and the fact table
--    6. rollups              hourly and daily aggregates
--    7. trend reports        window functions over the facts
--    8. gaps and islands     outages, empty hours, low-battery streaks
--    9. data quality         checks that must return zero rows
--   10. report suite         what operations reads every morning
--
--  Conventions: times are UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; every step can
--  be rerun for the same batch without changing the result.
-- =====================================================================

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Operational schema: the fleet as the operations team keeps it.
--    Normalised: each fact about the fleet is stored exactly once, and
--    the constraints refuse any row that could not be true.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE satellite (
  sat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (code GLOB 'ORB-[0-9]*'),
  name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  launched_on  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (launched_on IS date(launched_on)),
  status       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                       CHECK (status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  status_since TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status_since >= launched_on)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor_type (
  type_code  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CHECK (type_code = lower(type_code)),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT NOT NULL,
  min_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  max_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  CHECK (min_valid < max_valid)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor (
  sensor_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES sensor_type (type_code),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE ground_station (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (length(code) = 3 AND code = upper(code)),
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  latitude   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90),
  longitude  REAL NOT NULL CHECK (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180)
);

-- A planned contact: the satellite is above the station's horizon from
-- aos (acquisition of signal) until los (loss of signal).
CREATE TABLE contact_pass (
  pass_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_station (station_id),
  aos        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (aos IS datetime(aos, '+0 seconds')),
  los        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (los IS datetime(los, '+0 seconds')),
  CHECK (los > aos),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, aos)
);
