-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The star schema. Grain of the fact table: one reading of one
--    sensor at one moment. Dimensions use surrogate keys (sat_key,
--    sensor_key, time_key) so the warehouse does not depend on how the
--    operational tables number things.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: satellite.sat_id
  sat_code  TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: sensor.sensor_id
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,         -- copied in, so reports need no extra join
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_label TEXT    NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: ground_station.station_id
  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  station_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  hemisphere   TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (hemisphere IN ('N', 'S'))  -- derived from latitude
);

-- A calendar, one row per hour, with no holes: an hour with no readings
-- still has a row, which is how reports can show it as empty.
CREATE TABLE dim_time (
  time_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                               -- YYYYMMDDHH
  hour_start TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,                           -- '2026-03-01 14:00:00'
  day        TEXT    NOT NULL,                                  -- '2026-03-01'
  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),
  weekday    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Sunday
  shift      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (shift IN ('A', 'B', 'C'))  -- 00-08, 08-16, 16-24
);

CREATE TABLE fact_reading (
  reading_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  ts         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  value      REAL    NOT NULL,
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- lineage: the batch this version came from
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)       -- the grain, enforced
);

-- TODO (milestone 5): the tables fact_correction and etl_batch.

CREATE VIEW v_pipeline_monitor AS
SELECT NULL AS run_id, NULL AS batch_id, NULL AS staged, NULL AS clean, NULL AS rejected,
       NULL AS facts_owned, NULL AS corrections
WHERE 0;  -- TODO

-- The clean rows of every batch, one per sensor and moment: when a batch
-- holds the same reading twice, its last line wins.
CREATE VIEW v_stg_accepted AS
SELECT r.batch_id,
       r.line_no,
       d.sensor_key,
       CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', r.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time_key,
       r.ts,
       r.value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         sensor_id,
         ts,
         value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
                            ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE reject_reason IS NULL
) r
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_load AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'load'
BEGIN
  -- Dimensions first: a fact may only point at rows that exist.
  INSERT INTO dim_satellite (sat_id, sat_code, sat_name, status)
  SELECT sat_id, code, name, status
  FROM satellite
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY sat_id
  ON CONFLICT (sat_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_code = excluded.sat_code,
    sat_name = excluded.sat_name,
    status   = excluded.status;

  INSERT INTO dim_sensor (sensor_id, sat_key, sat_code, type_code, type_label, unit)
  SELECT se.sensor_id, ds.sat_key, ds.sat_code, st.type_code, st.label, st.unit
  FROM sensor se
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = se.sat_id
  JOIN sensor_type   st ON st.type_code = se.type_code
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY se.sensor_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_key    = excluded.sat_key,
    sat_code   = excluded.sat_code,
    type_label = excluded.type_label,
    unit       = excluded.unit;

  INSERT INTO dim_station (station_id, station_code, station_name, hemisphere)
  SELECT station_id, code, name, CASE WHEN latitude >= 0 THEN 'N' ELSE 'S' END
  FROM ground_station
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY station_id
  ON CONFLICT (station_id) DO UPDATE SET
    station_code = excluded.station_code,
    station_name = excluded.station_name,
    hemisphere   = excluded.hemisphere;

  -- The calendar: every hour from the earliest to the latest known reading.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (time_key, hour_start, day, hour, weekday, shift)
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         h,
         date(h),
         CAST(strftime('%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         CAST(strftime('%w', h) AS INTEGER),
         CASE WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '08' THEN 'A'
              WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '16' THEN 'B'
              ELSE 'C' END
  FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (
      SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours
      WHERE h < (SELECT MAX(last_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MAX(hour_start) AS last_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MAX(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL))
    )
    SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL
  );

  -- Facts: new readings only; a reading already in the warehouse stays.
  INSERT INTO fact_reading (sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no)
  SELECT sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no
  FROM v_stg_accepted
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO NOTHING;

  -- TODO (milestone 5): log corrections, change the upsert above so the
  -- newest batch wins, and record the batch in etl_batch.

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run the pipeline once for every batch in the landing zone, oldest first.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landing_packet
ORDER BY batch_id;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('staged', '1', 1382), ('staged', '2', 1322), ('staged', '3', 2706),
  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('quarantine', '1:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '1:malformed_json',    2),
  ('quarantine', '1:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '1:non_numeric_value', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_satellite', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_sensor',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:malformed_json',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '2:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '3:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:unknown_sensor',    1);

CREATE VIEW test_quarantine AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'quarantine') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT batch_id || ':' || reason AS item, packets AS actual
                 FROM v_quarantine_summary) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('facts', 'ORB-1', 1144), ('facts', 'ORB-2', 1137), ('facts', 'ORB-3', 1104),
  ('facts', 'ORB-4', 1148), ('facts', 'ORB-5', 846),
  ('dims', 'dim_satellite', 6), ('dims', 'dim_sensor', 23),
  ('dims', 'dim_station', 4),   ('dims', 'dim_time', 48);

CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test IN ('facts', 'dims')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'facts' AS test, d.sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading f
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_code
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_satellite', COUNT(*) FROM dim_satellite
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_sensor',    COUNT(*) FROM dim_sensor
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_station',   COUNT(*) FROM dim_station
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_time',      COUNT(*) FROM dim_time) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

-- TODO (milestone 5): the hand counts, expect_correction, and the views
-- test_lineage and test_corrections.
CREATE VIEW test_lineage AS
SELECT NULL AS item, NULL AS expected, NULL AS actual
WHERE 1;

CREATE VIEW test_corrections AS
SELECT NULL AS problem, NULL AS sat_code, NULL AS type_code, NULL AS ts
WHERE 1;

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
  UNION ALL SELECT 'lineage',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_lineage
  UNION ALL SELECT 'corrections',        COUNT(*)             FROM test_corrections
);
--- solution
-- =====================================================================
--  ORBIT fleet telemetry warehouse
--
--  One script builds the whole database from an empty file that holds
--  only the landing zone (landing_packet). The layers, in the order the
--  data flows through them:
--
--    1. operational schema   the fleet, as the operations team keeps it
--    2. pipeline control     runs and steps, one trigger per step
--    3. staging              every landed packet, parsed, not trusted
--    4. quarantine           rejected packets, each with one reason
--    5. star schema          dimensions and the fact table
--    6. rollups              hourly and daily aggregates
--    7. trend reports        window functions over the facts
--    8. gaps and islands     outages, empty hours, low-battery streaks
--    9. data quality         checks that must return zero rows
--   10. report suite         what operations reads every morning
--
--  Conventions: times are UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; every step can
--  be rerun for the same batch without changing the result.
-- =====================================================================

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Operational schema: the fleet as the operations team keeps it.
--    Normalised: each fact about the fleet is stored exactly once, and
--    the constraints refuse any row that could not be true.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE satellite (
  sat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (code GLOB 'ORB-[0-9]*'),
  name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  launched_on  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (launched_on IS date(launched_on)),
  status       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                       CHECK (status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  status_since TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status_since >= launched_on)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor_type (
  type_code  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CHECK (type_code = lower(type_code)),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT NOT NULL,
  min_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  max_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  CHECK (min_valid < max_valid)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor (
  sensor_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES sensor_type (type_code),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE ground_station (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (length(code) = 3 AND code = upper(code)),
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  latitude   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90),
  longitude  REAL NOT NULL CHECK (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180)
);

-- A planned contact: the satellite is above the station's horizon from
-- aos (acquisition of signal) until los (loss of signal).
CREATE TABLE contact_pass (
  pass_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_station (station_id),
  aos        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (aos IS datetime(aos, '+0 seconds')),
  los        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (los IS datetime(los, '+0 seconds')),
  CHECK (los > aos),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, aos)
);

-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The star schema. Grain of the fact table: one reading of one
--    sensor at one moment. Dimensions use surrogate keys (sat_key,
--    sensor_key, time_key) so the warehouse does not depend on how the
--    operational tables number things.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: satellite.sat_id
  sat_code  TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: sensor.sensor_id
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,         -- copied in, so reports need no extra join
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_label TEXT    NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: ground_station.station_id
  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  station_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  hemisphere   TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (hemisphere IN ('N', 'S'))  -- derived from latitude
);

-- A calendar, one row per hour, with no holes: an hour with no readings
-- still has a row, which is how reports can show it as empty.
CREATE TABLE dim_time (
  time_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                               -- YYYYMMDDHH
  hour_start TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,                           -- '2026-03-01 14:00:00'
  day        TEXT    NOT NULL,                                  -- '2026-03-01'
  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),
  weekday    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Sunday
  shift      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (shift IN ('A', 'B', 'C'))  -- 00-08, 08-16, 16-24
);

CREATE TABLE fact_reading (
  reading_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  ts         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  value      REAL    NOT NULL,
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- lineage: the batch this version came from
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)       -- the grain, enforced
);

-- Every time a newer batch changed a value that was already loaded.
CREATE TABLE fact_correction (
  correction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  ts            TEXT    NOT NULL,
  old_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  new_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  old_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  new_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (new_batch > old_batch),
  run_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id)
);

-- Which batches have been loaded, and how many times.
CREATE TABLE etl_batch (
  batch_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  first_run INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  last_run  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  runs      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (runs >= 1)
);

-- One row per run: what went into and came out of each step, side by side.
CREATE VIEW v_pipeline_monitor AS
SELECT r.run_id,
       r.batch_id,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'stage'    THEN s.rows_out END) AS staged,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_out END) AS clean,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_in - s.rows_out END) AS rejected,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'load'     THEN s.rows_out END) AS facts_owned,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_correction c WHERE c.run_id = r.run_id) AS corrections
FROM etl_run r
JOIN etl_step s ON s.run_id = r.run_id
GROUP BY r.run_id, r.batch_id;

-- The clean rows of every batch, one per sensor and moment: when a batch
-- holds the same reading twice, its last line wins.
CREATE VIEW v_stg_accepted AS
SELECT r.batch_id,
       r.line_no,
       d.sensor_key,
       CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', r.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time_key,
       r.ts,
       r.value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         sensor_id,
         ts,
         value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
                            ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE reject_reason IS NULL
) r
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_load AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'load'
BEGIN
  -- Dimensions first: a fact may only point at rows that exist.
  INSERT INTO dim_satellite (sat_id, sat_code, sat_name, status)
  SELECT sat_id, code, name, status
  FROM satellite
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY sat_id
  ON CONFLICT (sat_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_code = excluded.sat_code,
    sat_name = excluded.sat_name,
    status   = excluded.status;

  INSERT INTO dim_sensor (sensor_id, sat_key, sat_code, type_code, type_label, unit)
  SELECT se.sensor_id, ds.sat_key, ds.sat_code, st.type_code, st.label, st.unit
  FROM sensor se
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = se.sat_id
  JOIN sensor_type   st ON st.type_code = se.type_code
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY se.sensor_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_key    = excluded.sat_key,
    sat_code   = excluded.sat_code,
    type_label = excluded.type_label,
    unit       = excluded.unit;

  INSERT INTO dim_station (station_id, station_code, station_name, hemisphere)
  SELECT station_id, code, name, CASE WHEN latitude >= 0 THEN 'N' ELSE 'S' END
  FROM ground_station
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY station_id
  ON CONFLICT (station_id) DO UPDATE SET
    station_code = excluded.station_code,
    station_name = excluded.station_name,
    hemisphere   = excluded.hemisphere;

  -- The calendar: every hour from the earliest to the latest known reading.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (time_key, hour_start, day, hour, weekday, shift)
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         h,
         date(h),
         CAST(strftime('%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         CAST(strftime('%w', h) AS INTEGER),
         CASE WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '08' THEN 'A'
              WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '16' THEN 'B'
              ELSE 'C' END
  FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (
      SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours
      WHERE h < (SELECT MAX(last_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MAX(hour_start) AS last_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MAX(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL))
    )
    SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL
  );

  -- Log corrections before they are applied: a newer batch that brings a
  -- different value for a reading already loaded.
  INSERT INTO fact_correction (sensor_key, ts, old_value, new_value, old_batch, new_batch, run_id)
  SELECT f.sensor_key, f.ts, f.value, a.value, f.batch_id, a.batch_id, NEW.run_id
  FROM v_stg_accepted a
  JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = a.sensor_key AND f.ts = a.ts
  WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND a.batch_id > f.batch_id
    AND a.value <> f.value;

  -- Facts: the version from the newest batch wins, whatever order the
  -- batches are loaded in. Rerunning a batch changes nothing.
  INSERT INTO fact_reading (sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no)
  SELECT sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no
  FROM v_stg_accepted
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO UPDATE SET
    value    = excluded.value,
    batch_id = excluded.batch_id,
    line_no  = excluded.line_no
  WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_reading.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO etl_batch (batch_id, first_run, last_run, runs)
  VALUES (NEW.batch_id, NEW.run_id, NEW.run_id, 1)
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET
    last_run = excluded.last_run,
    runs     = runs + 1;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run the pipeline once for every batch in the landing zone, oldest first.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landing_packet
ORDER BY batch_id;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('staged', '1', 1382), ('staged', '2', 1322), ('staged', '3', 2706),
  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('quarantine', '1:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '1:malformed_json',    2),
  ('quarantine', '1:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '1:non_numeric_value', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_satellite', 1),
  ('quarantine', '1:unknown_sensor',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:malformed_json',    1),
  ('quarantine', '2:missing_field',     1),
  ('quarantine', '2:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:bad_timestamp',     2),
  ('quarantine', '3:out_of_range',      1),
  ('quarantine', '3:unknown_sensor',    1);

CREATE VIEW test_quarantine AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'quarantine') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT batch_id || ':' || reason AS item, packets AS actual
                 FROM v_quarantine_summary) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('facts', 'ORB-1', 1144), ('facts', 'ORB-2', 1137), ('facts', 'ORB-3', 1104),
  ('facts', 'ORB-4', 1148), ('facts', 'ORB-5', 846),
  ('dims', 'dim_satellite', 6), ('dims', 'dim_sensor', 23),
  ('dims', 'dim_station', 4),   ('dims', 'dim_time', 48);

CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test IN ('facts', 'dims')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'facts' AS test, d.sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading f
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_code
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_satellite', COUNT(*) FROM dim_satellite
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_sensor',    COUNT(*) FROM dim_sensor
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_station',   COUNT(*) FROM dim_station
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_time',      COUNT(*) FROM dim_time) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

-- nine readings of the morning as well as its own 1,308.
INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('lineage', '1', 1360), ('lineage', '2', 1317), ('lineage', '3', 2702);

CREATE TABLE expect_correction (
  sat_code  TEXT NOT NULL,
  type_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  ts        TEXT NOT NULL,
  old_value REAL NOT NULL,
  new_value REAL NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_code, type_code, ts)
);

INSERT INTO expect_correction (sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value) VALUES
  ('ORB-1', 'batt_v', '2026-03-01 10:50:00', 28.4, 28.35);

CREATE VIEW test_lineage AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'lineage') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_corrections AS
SELECT 'missing' AS problem, sat_code, type_code, ts FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value FROM expect_correction
  EXCEPT
  SELECT d.sat_code, d.type_code, c.ts, c.old_value, c.new_value
  FROM fact_correction c JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'unexpected', sat_code, type_code, ts FROM (
  SELECT d.sat_code, d.type_code, c.ts, c.old_value, c.new_value
  FROM fact_correction c JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key
  EXCEPT
  SELECT sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value FROM expect_correction);

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
  UNION ALL SELECT 'lineage',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_lineage
  UNION ALL SELECT 'corrections',        COUNT(*)             FROM test_corrections
);
--- hint
The correction insert joins `v_stg_accepted a` to `fact_reading f` on `sensor_key` and `ts`, keeping `a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND a.batch_id > f.batch_id AND a.value <> f.value`. It selects `f.value` as the old value and `a.value` as the new one.
--- hint
The upsert ends `ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id, line_no = excluded.line_no WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_reading.batch_id`. The batch record is another upsert: `ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET last_run = excluded.last_run, runs = runs + 1`.
--- hint
`v_pipeline_monitor` joins `etl_run` to `etl_step`, groups by run, and picks each step's numbers with `MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'stage' THEN s.rows_out END)`. `test_corrections` is two `EXCEPT`s, one each way, between `expect_correction` and `fact_correction` joined to `dim_sensor`.

+++ practice | Depot counts: the newest report wins
--- schema
CREATE TABLE stock (
  depot   TEXT    NOT NULL,
  part    TEXT    NOT NULL,
  qty     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  seq     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (depot, part)
);
CREATE TABLE report (
  seq   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  depot TEXT    NOT NULL,
  part  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  qty   INTEGER NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO report VALUES
  (1, 'D1', 'bolt', 500), (1, 'D1', 'nut', 800), (1, 'D2', 'bolt', 120),
  (2, 'D1', 'bolt', 480), (2, 'D2', 'nut', 60),
  (3, 'D1', 'bolt', 470);
CREATE TABLE apply_request (request_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, seq INTEGER NOT NULL);
--- task
Depots send stock counts in numbered reports, stored in `report (seq, depot, part, qty)`; a higher `seq` is a newer report. `stock (depot, part, qty, seq)` holds the current count of each part at each depot, and the report it came from.

Create the trigger `apply_report`: after a row is inserted into `apply_request`, apply that report's rows to `stock`. A new (depot, part) is inserted; an existing one is updated only when the report is **newer** than the one it came from. Reports may be applied in any order and more than once.

Then apply the reports in the order 3, 1, 2.
--- starter
CREATE TRIGGER apply_report AFTER INSERT ON apply_request
BEGIN
  INSERT OR REPLACE INTO stock (depot, part, qty, seq)
  SELECT depot, part, qty, seq FROM report WHERE seq = NEW.seq;
END;

INSERT INTO apply_request (seq) VALUES (3), (1), (2);
--- solution
CREATE TRIGGER apply_report AFTER INSERT ON apply_request
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO stock (depot, part, qty, seq)
  SELECT depot, part, qty, seq FROM report WHERE seq = NEW.seq
  ON CONFLICT (depot, part) DO UPDATE SET
    qty = excluded.qty,
    seq = excluded.seq
  WHERE excluded.seq > stock.seq;
END;

INSERT INTO apply_request (seq) VALUES (3), (1), (2);
--- hint
`INSERT OR REPLACE` makes the last report applied win, so applying report 1 after report 3 puts an old count back.
--- hint
Use an upsert whose update has its own condition: `ON CONFLICT (depot, part) DO UPDATE SET qty = excluded.qty, seq = excluded.seq WHERE excluded.seq > stock.seq`. The `SELECT` before it needs a `WHERE` anyway, so the `ON` is not mistaken for a join.
--- check query | Every count is from the newest report that mentions it
SELECT depot, part, qty, seq FROM stock ORDER BY depot, part
=> [["D1", "bolt", 470, 3], ["D1", "nut", 800, 1], ["D2", "bolt", 120, 1], ["D2", "nut", 60, 2]]
--- check query | Applying report 1 again changes nothing
INSERT INTO apply_request (seq) VALUES (1);
SELECT depot, part, qty, seq FROM stock ORDER BY depot, part
=> [["D1", "bolt", 470, 3], ["D1", "nut", 800, 1], ["D2", "bolt", 120, 1], ["D2", "nut", 60, 2]]
--- check query | A newer report 4 still gets through
INSERT INTO report VALUES (4, 'D2', 'bolt', 100);
INSERT INTO apply_request (seq) VALUES (4);
SELECT qty, seq FROM stock WHERE depot = 'D2' AND part = 'bolt'
=> [[100, 4]]

+++ practice | Log the change before you make it
--- schema
CREATE TABLE price (item TEXT PRIMARY KEY, cents INTEGER NOT NULL, version INTEGER NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO price VALUES ('valve', 1200, 1), ('seal', 80, 1), ('hose', 450, 2);
CREATE TABLE incoming (item TEXT NOT NULL, cents INTEGER NOT NULL, version INTEGER NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO incoming VALUES ('valve', 1250, 2), ('seal', 80, 2), ('hose', 400, 1), ('pump', 9900, 1);
CREATE TABLE price_change (
  item      TEXT    NOT NULL,
  old_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
  new_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
  old_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  new_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);
--- task
`price (item, cents, version)` holds current prices, and `incoming (item, cents, version)` a new price list. An incoming price replaces the current one only when its `version` is higher.

Write two statements, in this order:

1. Insert into `price_change` one row for every incoming price that **will** replace a current price and **changes** it: the item, the old and new cents, and the old and new versions. A newer version with the same price is not a change.
2. Apply `incoming` to `price` with an upsert: new items are inserted; existing ones are updated only by a higher version.
--- starter
INSERT INTO price (item, cents, version)
SELECT item, cents, version FROM incoming WHERE true
ON CONFLICT (item) DO UPDATE SET cents = excluded.cents, version = excluded.version
WHERE excluded.version > price.version;

INSERT INTO price_change (item, old_cents, new_cents, old_version, new_version)
SELECT p.item, p.cents, i.cents, p.version, i.version
FROM incoming i JOIN price p ON p.item = i.item
WHERE i.version > p.version AND i.cents <> p.cents;
--- solution
INSERT INTO price_change (item, old_cents, new_cents, old_version, new_version)
SELECT p.item, p.cents, i.cents, p.version, i.version
FROM incoming i
JOIN price p ON p.item = i.item
WHERE i.version > p.version AND i.cents <> p.cents;

INSERT INTO price (item, cents, version)
SELECT item, cents, version FROM incoming WHERE true
ON CONFLICT (item) DO UPDATE SET cents = excluded.cents, version = excluded.version
WHERE excluded.version > price.version;
--- hint
The starter logs nothing. By the time its second statement runs, the upsert has already overwritten the old prices, so nothing looks older any more.
--- hint
Swap the two statements: find the changes while the old prices are still in `price`, then apply the upsert.
--- check query | One real change: the valve

+++ practice | Which batches still need loading
--- schema

--- task
`landed (batch_id, line_no)` holds every landed line, and `loaded_batch (batch_id, runs)` every batch the pipeline has loaded. Batch 4 arrived late, after batch 5 was loaded.

1. Create the view `pending (batch_id)`: every batch that has landed but has never been loaded, once each.
2. Create the trigger `mark_loaded` on a new table `load_done (batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL)`: after a row is inserted into `load_done`, record that batch in `loaded_batch`, with `runs` = 1 for a new batch and one more than before for a batch already there.

A "load everything above the highest loaded batch" rule would never see batch 4; your view must.
--- starter
CREATE VIEW pending AS
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id FROM landed
WHERE batch_id > (SELECT MAX(batch_id) FROM loaded_batch);

CREATE TABLE load_done (batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL);
--- solution
CREATE VIEW pending AS
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landed
WHERE batch_id NOT IN (SELECT batch_id FROM loaded_batch);

CREATE TABLE load_done (batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TRIGGER mark_loaded AFTER INSERT ON load_done
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO loaded_batch (batch_id, runs) VALUES (NEW.batch_id, 1)
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET runs = runs + 1;
END;
--- hint
Compare against the set of loaded batches, not against its maximum: a batch is pending when it is `NOT IN` the loaded ones.
--- hint
The trigger is one upsert: `INSERT INTO loaded_batch (batch_id, runs) VALUES (NEW.batch_id, 1) ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET runs = runs + 1`.

+++ practice | Same value, newer batch: not a correction
--- schema
CREATE TABLE fact (sensor TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (sensor, ts));

--- task
Readings are loaded from `incoming (sensor, ts, value, batch_id)` into `fact (sensor, ts, value, batch_id)`, where the highest `batch_id` wins. Create the trigger `load_incoming`: after a row is inserted into `load_request`,

1. log into `correction` every incoming reading that is from a **newer** batch than the fact **and** has a **different** value;
2. upsert all of `incoming` into `fact`, updating `value` and `batch_id` only when the incoming batch is newer.

The checks put readings into `incoming` and insert into `load_request`. An exact re-send from a newer batch moves the fact to that batch but is not a correction; an older batch never changes anything; loading the same readings twice logs nothing new.
--- starter
CREATE TRIGGER load_incoming AFTER INSERT ON load_request
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO correction
  SELECT f.sensor, f.ts, f.value, i.value, f.batch_id, i.batch_id
  FROM incoming i JOIN fact f ON f.sensor = i.sensor AND f.ts = i.ts
  WHERE i.batch_id >= f.batch_id;
  INSERT INTO fact (sensor, ts, value, batch_id)
  SELECT sensor, ts, value, batch_id FROM incoming WHERE true
  ON CONFLICT (sensor, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id;
END;
--- solution
CREATE TRIGGER load_incoming AFTER INSERT ON load_request
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO correction
  SELECT f.sensor, f.ts, f.value, i.value, f.batch_id, i.batch_id
  FROM incoming i
  JOIN fact f ON f.sensor = i.sensor AND f.ts = i.ts
  WHERE i.batch_id > f.batch_id AND i.value <> f.value;

  SELECT sensor, ts, value, batch_id FROM incoming WHERE true
  ON CONFLICT (sensor, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id

--- hint
Three edges: a re-send from the same batch (not newer), a re-send from a newer batch with the same value (newer but not different), and an older batch (never applied). The log condition needs both "newer" and "different"; the upsert needs "newer".

ON CONFLICT (sensor, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_x.batch_id;

INSERT INTO fact_y SELECT sensor, ts, value, batch_id FROM stg WHERE batch_id = 3
ON CONFLICT (sensor, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_y.batch_id;
INSERT INTO fact_y SELECT sensor, ts, value, batch_id FROM stg WHERE batch_id = 1
ON CONFLICT (sensor, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_y.batch_id;

ON CONFLICT (sensor, ts) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, batch_id = excluded.batch_id WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_y.batch_id;

CREATE VIEW order_diff AS
SELECT sensor, ts FROM (SELECT * FROM fact_x EXCEPT SELECT * FROM fact_y)
UNION
SELECT sensor, ts FROM (SELECT * FROM fact_y EXCEPT SELECT * FROM fact_x);

=== cap-data-06 | Data system 6: rollups kept up to date
--- teach
Last milestone made the load safe to rerun and to run in any order. The fact table now holds the truth, one reading at a time. But most questions are not about one reading: "the hourly average", "the daily low", "how many readings did ORB-3 send on Sunday". This milestone builds **rollups**, small summary tables that answer those questions without reading every fact, and keeps them correct as batches arrive late, twice, or with corrections.

### What a rollup is

A **rollup** (also called an aggregate table or a summary table) stores the result of a `GROUP BY` so that it does not have to be [[run again|materialized]]. `agg_sensor_hour` has one row per sensor and hour: the number of readings `n`, `min_value`, `max_value` and `sum_value`. Here it has about 900 rows for 5,379 facts. A year of telemetry would have millions of facts and a few hundred thousand rollup rows, and a dashboard reading the rollup never touches the facts at all.

### Store the sum, not the average

The average is the number people want, so why not store it? Because a rollup must be **rolled up again**: hours into days, days into months. A count and a sum combine by adding them. Averages do not:

| hour | readings | average |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13:00 | 6 | 31.0 |
| 14:00 | 0 | (none) |
| 15:00 | 2 | 35.0 |

The day's average over those hours is (6 × 31.0 + 2 × 35.0) / 8 = 32.0. The average of the two hourly averages is 33.0, which weighs a half-empty hour like a full one. So the rollup stores `n` and `sum_value`, and the views divide: `sum_value / n` for an hour, `SUM(sum_value) / SUM(n)` for a day. Count, sum, min and max all combine this way, so they can be [[rolled up any number of times|distributive]]. A median cannot: the median of medians is not the median.

### Keeping it up to date

When batch 4 lands, which rollup rows change? Three designs:

1. **Rebuild everything** from the facts on every run. Simple, and always right, but the cost grows with the whole history, every run.
2. **Add the batch's numbers** to the existing rows: `n = n + …`, `sum_value = sum_value + …`. Fast, and wrong three ways. A rerun adds the batch twice. A correction must subtract the old value, which the rollup no longer knows. And a maximum can go up, but it can never come down again.
3. **Recompute the touched cells.** Find the (sensor, hour) cells this batch has readings in, delete their rollup rows, and compute them again from the facts. **Chosen.**

The touched cells are the (`sensor_key`, `time_key`) pairs of the batch's rows in `v_stg_accepted`. That includes a late reading from an old hour, and a correction: both touch the old hour, so it is recomputed.

```sql fragment
DELETE FROM summary
WHERE (thing, hour) IN (SELECT thing, hour FROM this_batch);
```

That is a **row value**: `(a, b) IN (SELECT x, y …)` compares pairs, so one condition finds exactly the touched cells.

### Why it is correct

The invariant: every rollup row equals the `GROUP BY` of the facts for its cell, and every cell with facts has a row. A load changes facts only at the keys of its batch, and all those keys lie in the batch's touched cells. So after the rollup step recomputes those cells from the final facts, they are right; every other cell had no fact change, so it was right before and still is. Recomputing a cell twice gives the same row, so the step is idempotent, and it does not care which batch came first.

### A second level: satellite days

The morning report wants one row per satellite and day, with its readings, how many sensors reported, and the day's extremes side by side: the lowest battery voltage, the hottest flight computer, the coldest and hottest solar panel. `agg_satellite_day` stores that, rolled up from the hours, not from the facts. The same recompute rule applies one level up: after the hours, recompute the (satellite, day) cells the batch touched.

Putting different sensors' numbers side by side is conditional aggregation, the pivot from the expert course: `MIN(CASE WHEN type_code = 'batt_v' THEN min_value END)` is the lowest battery reading, because the `CASE` gives NULL for every other sensor and `MIN` skips NULLs.

### A second fact table: passes

A ground station pass is an event of its own, with its own grain: **one planned pass**. `fact_pass` records, for each pass, how long it was planned for and what the station actually heard while the satellite was overhead: the number of readings with `aos <= ts < los`, and the first and last of them. A pass with `readings_heard = 0` is a **lost pass**.

It shares `dim_satellite` and `dim_time` with `fact_reading`. Dimensions shared by several fact tables are called [[conformed dimensions|conformed]], and they are what lets one report put readings and passes side by side.

Which passes does a batch touch? A pass can gain readings only if it overlaps the stretch of time the batch covers, from its earliest to its latest accepted reading. So the step recomputes every pass that overlaps that stretch. A pass must be recomputed even when it heard nothing, so the readings come in through a `LEFT JOIN`, and the pass's hour must already be in the calendar. `INSERT OR REPLACE` writes each pass's row whether or not it existed.

### The rollup step

```text
rollup(batch b):
  cells = the (sensor_key, time_key) of b's accepted rows
  delete and recompute agg_sensor_hour for cells, from fact_reading
  days  = the (sat_key, day) of those cells
  delete and recompute agg_satellite_day for days, from agg_sensor_hour
  recompute fact_pass for every pass overlapping b's time span
  log: rows_in = b's accepted rows, rows_out = number of cells
```

### What it costs

The step does work in proportion to the cells the batch touched and the facts inside them: an hour holds at most 6 readings per sensor, so recomputing k cells reads about 6k facts. A full rebuild would read all F facts. For a batch of one day, k is about 450 and F grows by a day's readings with every batch, so the gap widens every day the system runs.

### How to test it

The hand counts are the readings per satellite per day, from the slots each satellite missed, and the passes: 30 planned, 5 lost. ORB-5's two readings that arrived late in batch 3 belong to 23:00 on 1 March, so that hour must say 4 readings, not 2. The checks also land a correction for an old hour and rerun batches.

**Watch out:** do not pick the touched cells from `fact_reading WHERE batch_id = b`. After the load, a reading re-sent by batch b belongs to b, but a reading where b sent an *older* version than the one already there still belongs to the newer batch. The cells to recompute are the cells b *sent* readings for, which is what `v_stg_accepted` holds.

::: context materialized Views that store their answer
A view reruns its query every time. A **materialized view**, available in PostgreSQL and Oracle, stores its result like a table and is refreshed on demand, often by rerunning the whole query. SQLite has no materialized views, so the rollups here are ordinary tables kept current by the pipeline. The recompute-the-touched-cells step is what databases that support it call incremental refresh, and it is why the rollups stay cheap as the history grows.
:::

::: context distributive Aggregates that combine
Statisticians sort aggregates by whether they can be computed in pieces. Count, sum, minimum and maximum are **distributive**: the total of the pieces' totals is the total. The average is **algebraic**: it cannot be combined directly, but it can be rebuilt from two distributive pieces, sum and count. That is why the rollup stores those two. The median is **holistic**: no fixed set of numbers per piece is enough, and it needs all the values. Rollups can serve the first two kinds cheaply, and not the third.
:::

::: context conformed Dimensions that mean the same thing everywhere
Two fact tables can only be compared if they describe the world with the same dimensions. If readings used an hour dimension and passes used their own separate calendar with different keys, a report that joins "readings per hour" to "passes per hour" would have to match the two by hand. Kimball calls a dimension used by several fact tables a **conformed dimension**, and planning them is most of the work of designing a warehouse. Here `dim_time` and `dim_satellite` are conformed; `dim_station` so far serves only passes.
:::
--- task
The tables `agg_sensor_hour`, `agg_satellite_day` and `fact_pass` are in the starter, and `'rollup'` has been added to the steps of a run. Write:

1. The trigger `etl_rollup`, after a row is inserted into `etl_step` whose `step` is `'rollup'`. For that row's batch:
   - delete the `agg_sensor_hour` rows whose (`sensor_key`, `time_key`) is among the batch's rows in `v_stg_accepted`, then insert those cells again from `fact_reading`: `n` = `COUNT(*)`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `sum_value`;
   - delete the `agg_satellite_day` rows whose (`sat_key`, `day`) belongs to those cells, then insert them again from `agg_sensor_hour`: `readings` = the sum of `n`, `sensors` = the number of distinct sensors, `min_batt_v` = the lowest `min_value` of `batt_v` sensors, `max_cpu_t` = the highest `max_value` of `cpu_t` sensors, `min_panel_t` and `max_panel_t` the same for `panel_t`;
   - write with `INSERT OR REPLACE` a `fact_pass` row for every pass in `contact_pass` whose `los` is after the batch's earliest accepted `ts` and whose `aos` is not after its latest accepted `ts`, and whose `aos` hour is in `dim_time`: `pass_id`, the satellite's `sat_key`, the station's `station_key`, the `time_key` of the `aos` hour, `planned_minutes` = whole minutes from `aos` to `los`, `readings_heard` = the satellite's facts with `aos <= ts < los`, and the first and last `ts` of them (NULL when none);
   - set the step row's `rows_in` to the batch's rows in `v_stg_accepted` and `rows_out` to the number of distinct (`sensor_key`, `time_key`) among them.
2. The view `v_sensor_hour (sat_code, type_code, time_key, hour_start, n, min_value, max_value, avg_value)`, one row per rollup row, with `avg_value = ROUND(sum_value / n, 3)`.
3. The view `v_sensor_day (sat_code, type_code, day, n, min_value, max_value, avg_value)`, one row per sensor and day, rolled up from `agg_sensor_hour`, with `avg_value = ROUND(SUM(sum_value) / SUM(n), 3)`.
4. The test: insert the ten daily hand counts with test `'day'` and item `'<sat_code> <day>'`: ORB-1 576 and 568, ORB-2 577 and 560, ORB-3 528 and 576, ORB-4 576 and 572, ORB-5 426 and 420 (1 March, then 2 March), and `('pass_fact', 'planned', 30)`, `('pass_fact', 'lost', 5)`. Replace the stub `test_rollup (item, expected, actual)` with a view that compares them with `agg_satellite_day` and with the number of `fact_pass` rows and of rows with `readings_heard = 0`.
--- starter
-- =====================================================================
--  ORBIT fleet telemetry warehouse
--
--  One script builds the whole database from an empty file that holds
--  only the landing zone (landing_packet). The layers, in the order the
--  data flows through them:
--
--    1. operational schema   the fleet, as the operations team keeps it
--    2. pipeline control     runs and steps, one trigger per step
--    3. staging              every landed packet, parsed, not trusted
--    4. quarantine           rejected packets, each with one reason
--    5. star schema          dimensions and the fact table
--    6. rollups              hourly and daily aggregates
--    7. trend reports        window functions over the facts
--    8. gaps and islands     outages, empty hours, low-battery streaks
--    9. data quality         checks that must return zero rows
--   10. report suite         what operations reads every morning
--
--  Conventions: times are UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; every step can
--  be rerun for the same batch without changing the result.
-- =====================================================================

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Operational schema: the fleet as the operations team keeps it.
--    Normalised: each fact about the fleet is stored exactly once, and
--    the constraints refuse any row that could not be true.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE satellite (
  sat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (code GLOB 'ORB-[0-9]*'),
  name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  launched_on  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (launched_on IS date(launched_on)),
  status       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                       CHECK (status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  status_since TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status_since >= launched_on)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor_type (
  type_code  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CHECK (type_code = lower(type_code)),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT NOT NULL,
  min_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  max_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  CHECK (min_valid < max_valid)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor (
  sensor_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES sensor_type (type_code),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE ground_station (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (length(code) = 3 AND code = upper(code)),
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  latitude   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90),
  longitude  REAL NOT NULL CHECK (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180)
);

-- A planned contact: the satellite is above the station's horizon from
-- aos (acquisition of signal) until los (loss of signal).
CREATE TABLE contact_pass (
  pass_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_station (station_id),
  aos        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (aos IS datetime(aos, '+0 seconds')),
  los        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (los IS datetime(los, '+0 seconds')),
  CHECK (los > aos),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, aos)
);
