-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load', 'rollup')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'rollup');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The star schema. Grain of the fact table: one reading of one
--    sensor at one moment. Dimensions use surrogate keys (sat_key,
--    sensor_key, time_key) so the warehouse does not depend on how the
--    operational tables number things.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: satellite.sat_id
  sat_code  TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: sensor.sensor_id
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,         -- copied in, so reports need no extra join
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_label TEXT    NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: ground_station.station_id
  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  station_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  hemisphere   TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (hemisphere IN ('N', 'S'))  -- derived from latitude
);

-- A calendar, one row per hour, with no holes: an hour with no readings
-- still has a row, which is how reports can show it as empty.
CREATE TABLE dim_time (
  time_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                               -- YYYYMMDDHH
  hour_start TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,                           -- '2026-03-01 14:00:00'
  day        TEXT    NOT NULL,                                  -- '2026-03-01'
  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),
  weekday    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Sunday
  shift      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (shift IN ('A', 'B', 'C'))  -- 00-08, 08-16, 16-24
);

CREATE TABLE fact_reading (
  reading_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  ts         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  value      REAL    NOT NULL,
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- lineage: the batch this version came from
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)       -- the grain, enforced
);

-- Every time a newer batch changed a value that was already loaded.
CREATE TABLE fact_correction (
  correction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  ts            TEXT    NOT NULL,
  old_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  new_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  old_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  new_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (new_batch > old_batch),
  run_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id)
);

-- Which batches have been loaded, and how many times.
CREATE TABLE etl_batch (
  batch_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  first_run INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  last_run  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  runs      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (runs >= 1)
);

-- One row per run: what went into and came out of each step, side by side.
CREATE VIEW v_pipeline_monitor AS
SELECT r.run_id,
       r.batch_id,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'stage'    THEN s.rows_out END) AS staged,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_out END) AS clean,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_in - s.rows_out END) AS rejected,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'load'     THEN s.rows_out END) AS facts_owned,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_correction c WHERE c.run_id = r.run_id) AS corrections
FROM etl_run r
JOIN etl_step s ON s.run_id = r.run_id
GROUP BY r.run_id, r.batch_id;

-- The clean rows of every batch, one per sensor and moment: when a batch
-- holds the same reading twice, its last line wins.
CREATE VIEW v_stg_accepted AS
SELECT r.batch_id,
       r.line_no,
       d.sensor_key,
       CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', r.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time_key,
       r.ts,
       r.value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         sensor_id,
         ts,
         value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
                            ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE reject_reason IS NULL
) r
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_load AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'load'
BEGIN
  -- Dimensions first: a fact may only point at rows that exist.
  INSERT INTO dim_satellite (sat_id, sat_code, sat_name, status)
  SELECT sat_id, code, name, status
  FROM satellite
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY sat_id
  ON CONFLICT (sat_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_code = excluded.sat_code,
    sat_name = excluded.sat_name,
    status   = excluded.status;

  INSERT INTO dim_sensor (sensor_id, sat_key, sat_code, type_code, type_label, unit)
  SELECT se.sensor_id, ds.sat_key, ds.sat_code, st.type_code, st.label, st.unit
  FROM sensor se
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = se.sat_id
  JOIN sensor_type   st ON st.type_code = se.type_code
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY se.sensor_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_key    = excluded.sat_key,
    sat_code   = excluded.sat_code,
    type_label = excluded.type_label,
    unit       = excluded.unit;

  INSERT INTO dim_station (station_id, station_code, station_name, hemisphere)
  SELECT station_id, code, name, CASE WHEN latitude >= 0 THEN 'N' ELSE 'S' END
  FROM ground_station
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY station_id
  ON CONFLICT (station_id) DO UPDATE SET
    station_code = excluded.station_code,
    station_name = excluded.station_name,
    hemisphere   = excluded.hemisphere;

  -- The calendar: every hour from the earliest to the latest known reading.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (time_key, hour_start, day, hour, weekday, shift)
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         h,
         date(h),
         CAST(strftime('%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         CAST(strftime('%w', h) AS INTEGER),
         CASE WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '08' THEN 'A'
              WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '16' THEN 'B'
              ELSE 'C' END
  FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (
      SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours
      WHERE h < (SELECT MAX(last_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MAX(hour_start) AS last_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MAX(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL))
    )
    SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL
  );

  -- Log corrections before they are applied: a newer batch that brings a
  -- different value for a reading already loaded.
  INSERT INTO fact_correction (sensor_key, ts, old_value, new_value, old_batch, new_batch, run_id)
  SELECT f.sensor_key, f.ts, f.value, a.value, f.batch_id, a.batch_id, NEW.run_id
  FROM v_stg_accepted a
  JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = a.sensor_key AND f.ts = a.ts
  WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND a.batch_id > f.batch_id
    AND a.value <> f.value;

  -- Facts: the version from the newest batch wins, whatever order the
  -- batches are loaded in. Rerunning a batch changes nothing.
  INSERT INTO fact_reading (sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no)
  SELECT sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no
  FROM v_stg_accepted
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO UPDATE SET
    value    = excluded.value,
    batch_id = excluded.batch_id,
    line_no  = excluded.line_no
  WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_reading.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO etl_batch (batch_id, first_run, last_run, runs)
  VALUES (NEW.batch_id, NEW.run_id, NEW.run_id, 1)
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET
    last_run = excluded.last_run,
    runs     = runs + 1;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. Rollups (milestone 6).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE agg_sensor_hour (
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  n          INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (n > 0),
  min_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  max_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  sum_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sensor_key, time_key)
);

CREATE TABLE agg_satellite_day (
  sat_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  day         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  readings    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (readings > 0),
  sensors     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  min_batt_v  REAL,
  max_cpu_t   REAL,
  min_panel_t REAL,
  max_panel_t REAL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_key, day)
);

CREATE TABLE fact_pass (
  pass_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_key         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  station_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_station (station_key),
  time_key        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  planned_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (planned_minutes > 0),
  readings_heard  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (readings_heard >= 0),
  first_heard     TEXT,
  last_heard      TEXT
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_rollup AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'rollup'
BEGIN
  SELECT 'TODO: recompute the hours, the days and the passes this batch touched';
END;

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)

FROM landing_packet

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('staged', '1', 1382), ('staged', '2', 1322), ('staged', '3', 2706),
  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_quarantine AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'quarantine') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT batch_id || ':' || reason AS item, packets AS actual
                 FROM v_quarantine_summary) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('facts', 'ORB-1', 1144), ('facts', 'ORB-2', 1137), ('facts', 'ORB-3', 1104),
  ('facts', 'ORB-4', 1148), ('facts', 'ORB-5', 846),
  ('dims', 'dim_satellite', 6), ('dims', 'dim_sensor', 23),
  ('dims', 'dim_station', 4),   ('dims', 'dim_time', 48);

CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test IN ('facts', 'dims')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'facts' AS test, d.sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading f
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_code
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_satellite', COUNT(*) FROM dim_satellite
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_sensor',    COUNT(*) FROM dim_sensor
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_station',   COUNT(*) FROM dim_station
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_time',      COUNT(*) FROM dim_time) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE TABLE expect_correction (
  sat_code  TEXT NOT NULL,
  type_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  ts        TEXT NOT NULL,
  old_value REAL NOT NULL,
  new_value REAL NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_code, type_code, ts)
);

CREATE VIEW test_lineage AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'lineage') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_corrections AS
SELECT 'missing' AS problem, sat_code, type_code, ts FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value FROM expect_correction
  EXCEPT
  SELECT d.sat_code, d.type_code, c.ts, c.old_value, c.new_value
  FROM fact_correction c JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'unexpected', sat_code, type_code, ts FROM (
  SELECT d.sat_code, d.type_code, c.ts, c.old_value, c.new_value
  FROM fact_correction c JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key
  EXCEPT
  SELECT sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value FROM expect_correction);

SELECT NULL AS item, NULL AS expected, NULL AS actual
WHERE 1;

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
  UNION ALL SELECT 'lineage',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_lineage
  UNION ALL SELECT 'corrections',        COUNT(*)             FROM test_corrections
  UNION ALL SELECT 'rollup',             COUNT(*)             FROM test_rollup
);
--- solution
-- =====================================================================
--  ORBIT fleet telemetry warehouse
--
--  One script builds the whole database from an empty file that holds
--  only the landing zone (landing_packet). The layers, in the order the
--  data flows through them:
--
--    1. operational schema   the fleet, as the operations team keeps it
--    2. pipeline control     runs and steps, one trigger per step
--    3. staging              every landed packet, parsed, not trusted
--    4. quarantine           rejected packets, each with one reason
--    5. star schema          dimensions and the fact table
--    6. rollups              hourly and daily aggregates
--    7. trend reports        window functions over the facts
--    8. gaps and islands     outages, empty hours, low-battery streaks
--    9. data quality         checks that must return zero rows
--   10. report suite         what operations reads every morning
--
--  Conventions: times are UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; every step can
--  be rerun for the same batch without changing the result.
-- =====================================================================

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Operational schema: the fleet as the operations team keeps it.
--    Normalised: each fact about the fleet is stored exactly once, and
--    the constraints refuse any row that could not be true.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE satellite (
  sat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (code GLOB 'ORB-[0-9]*'),
  name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  launched_on  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (launched_on IS date(launched_on)),
  status       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                       CHECK (status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  status_since TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status_since >= launched_on)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor_type (
  type_code  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CHECK (type_code = lower(type_code)),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT NOT NULL,
  min_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  max_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  CHECK (min_valid < max_valid)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor (
  sensor_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES sensor_type (type_code),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE ground_station (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (length(code) = 3 AND code = upper(code)),
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  latitude   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90),
  longitude  REAL NOT NULL CHECK (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180)
);

-- A planned contact: the satellite is above the station's horizon from
-- aos (acquisition of signal) until los (loss of signal).
CREATE TABLE contact_pass (
  pass_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_station (station_id),
  aos        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (aos IS datetime(aos, '+0 seconds')),
  los        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (los IS datetime(los, '+0 seconds')),
  CHECK (los > aos),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, aos)
);

-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load', 'rollup')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'rollup');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The star schema. Grain of the fact table: one reading of one
--    sensor at one moment. Dimensions use surrogate keys (sat_key,
--    sensor_key, time_key) so the warehouse does not depend on how the
--    operational tables number things.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: satellite.sat_id
  sat_code  TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: sensor.sensor_id
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,         -- copied in, so reports need no extra join
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_label TEXT    NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: ground_station.station_id
  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  station_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  hemisphere   TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (hemisphere IN ('N', 'S'))  -- derived from latitude
);

-- A calendar, one row per hour, with no holes: an hour with no readings
-- still has a row, which is how reports can show it as empty.
CREATE TABLE dim_time (
  time_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                               -- YYYYMMDDHH
  hour_start TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,                           -- '2026-03-01 14:00:00'
  day        TEXT    NOT NULL,                                  -- '2026-03-01'
  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),
  weekday    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Sunday
  shift      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (shift IN ('A', 'B', 'C'))  -- 00-08, 08-16, 16-24
);

CREATE TABLE fact_reading (
  reading_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  ts         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  value      REAL    NOT NULL,
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- lineage: the batch this version came from
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)       -- the grain, enforced
);

-- Every time a newer batch changed a value that was already loaded.
CREATE TABLE fact_correction (
  correction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  ts            TEXT    NOT NULL,
  old_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  new_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  old_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  new_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (new_batch > old_batch),
  run_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id)
);

-- Which batches have been loaded, and how many times.
CREATE TABLE etl_batch (
  batch_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  first_run INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  last_run  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  runs      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (runs >= 1)
);

-- One row per run: what went into and came out of each step, side by side.
CREATE VIEW v_pipeline_monitor AS
SELECT r.run_id,
       r.batch_id,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'stage'    THEN s.rows_out END) AS staged,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_out END) AS clean,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_in - s.rows_out END) AS rejected,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'load'     THEN s.rows_out END) AS facts_owned,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_correction c WHERE c.run_id = r.run_id) AS corrections
FROM etl_run r
JOIN etl_step s ON s.run_id = r.run_id
GROUP BY r.run_id, r.batch_id;

-- The clean rows of every batch, one per sensor and moment: when a batch
-- holds the same reading twice, its last line wins.
CREATE VIEW v_stg_accepted AS
SELECT r.batch_id,
       r.line_no,
       d.sensor_key,
       CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', r.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time_key,
       r.ts,
       r.value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         sensor_id,
         ts,
         value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
                            ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE reject_reason IS NULL
) r
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_load AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'load'
BEGIN
  -- Dimensions first: a fact may only point at rows that exist.
  INSERT INTO dim_satellite (sat_id, sat_code, sat_name, status)
  SELECT sat_id, code, name, status
  FROM satellite
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY sat_id
  ON CONFLICT (sat_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_code = excluded.sat_code,
    sat_name = excluded.sat_name,
    status   = excluded.status;

  INSERT INTO dim_sensor (sensor_id, sat_key, sat_code, type_code, type_label, unit)
  SELECT se.sensor_id, ds.sat_key, ds.sat_code, st.type_code, st.label, st.unit
  FROM sensor se
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = se.sat_id
  JOIN sensor_type   st ON st.type_code = se.type_code
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY se.sensor_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_key    = excluded.sat_key,
    sat_code   = excluded.sat_code,
    type_label = excluded.type_label,
    unit       = excluded.unit;

  INSERT INTO dim_station (station_id, station_code, station_name, hemisphere)
  SELECT station_id, code, name, CASE WHEN latitude >= 0 THEN 'N' ELSE 'S' END
  FROM ground_station
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY station_id
  ON CONFLICT (station_id) DO UPDATE SET
    station_code = excluded.station_code,
    station_name = excluded.station_name,
    hemisphere   = excluded.hemisphere;

  -- The calendar: every hour from the earliest to the latest known reading.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (time_key, hour_start, day, hour, weekday, shift)
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         h,
         date(h),
         CAST(strftime('%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         CAST(strftime('%w', h) AS INTEGER),
         CASE WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '08' THEN 'A'
              WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '16' THEN 'B'
              ELSE 'C' END
  FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (
      SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours
      WHERE h < (SELECT MAX(last_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MAX(hour_start) AS last_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MAX(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL))
    )
    SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL
  );

  -- Log corrections before they are applied: a newer batch that brings a
  -- different value for a reading already loaded.
  INSERT INTO fact_correction (sensor_key, ts, old_value, new_value, old_batch, new_batch, run_id)
  SELECT f.sensor_key, f.ts, f.value, a.value, f.batch_id, a.batch_id, NEW.run_id
  FROM v_stg_accepted a
  JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = a.sensor_key AND f.ts = a.ts
  WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND a.batch_id > f.batch_id
    AND a.value <> f.value;

  -- Facts: the version from the newest batch wins, whatever order the
  -- batches are loaded in. Rerunning a batch changes nothing.
  INSERT INTO fact_reading (sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no)
  SELECT sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no
  FROM v_stg_accepted
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO UPDATE SET
    value    = excluded.value,
    batch_id = excluded.batch_id,
    line_no  = excluded.line_no
  WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_reading.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO etl_batch (batch_id, first_run, last_run, runs)
  VALUES (NEW.batch_id, NEW.run_id, NEW.run_id, 1)
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET
    last_run = excluded.last_run,
    runs     = runs + 1;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. Rollups, kept up to date one batch at a time. Sums and counts are
--    stored, not averages, so a rollup can be rolled up again.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE agg_sensor_hour (
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  n          INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (n > 0),
  min_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  max_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  sum_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sensor_key, time_key)
);

-- One row per satellite and day, rolled up from the hours: the health
-- numbers the morning report needs, side by side.
CREATE TABLE agg_satellite_day (
  sat_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  day         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  readings    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (readings > 0),
  sensors     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  min_batt_v  REAL,
  max_cpu_t   REAL,
  min_panel_t REAL,
  max_panel_t REAL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_key, day)
);

-- A second fact table on the same dimensions. Grain: one planned pass.
-- It records what the station actually heard while the satellite was
-- overhead; readings_heard = 0 is a lost pass.
CREATE TABLE fact_pass (
  pass_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,  -- degenerate key: contact_pass.pass_id
  sat_key         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  station_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_station (station_key),
  time_key        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),  -- hour of aos
  planned_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (planned_minutes > 0),
  readings_heard  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (readings_heard >= 0),
  first_heard     TEXT,
  last_heard      TEXT
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_rollup AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'rollup'
BEGIN
  -- Recompute only the hours this batch touched, from the facts, so a
  -- late or corrected reading lands in the right hour and a rerun is harmless.
  DELETE FROM agg_sensor_hour
  WHERE (sensor_key, time_key) IN (SELECT sensor_key, time_key
                                   FROM v_stg_accepted
                                   WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id);

  INSERT INTO agg_sensor_hour (sensor_key, time_key, n, min_value, max_value, sum_value)
  SELECT sensor_key,
         time_key,
         COUNT(*),
         MIN(value),
         MAX(value),
         SUM(value)
  FROM fact_reading
  WHERE (sensor_key, time_key) IN (SELECT sensor_key, time_key
                                   FROM v_stg_accepted
                                   WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY sensor_key, time_key;

  -- Then the days those hours belong to, from the hours.
  DELETE FROM agg_satellite_day
  WHERE (sat_key, day) IN (SELECT d.sat_key, t.day
                           FROM v_stg_accepted a
                           JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
                           JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key
                           WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id);

  INSERT INTO agg_satellite_day (sat_key, day, readings, sensors,
                                 min_batt_v, max_cpu_t, min_panel_t, max_panel_t)
  SELECT d.sat_key,
         t.day,
         SUM(h.n),
         COUNT(DISTINCT h.sensor_key),
         MIN(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'batt_v'  THEN h.min_value END),
         MAX(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'cpu_t'   THEN h.max_value END),
         MIN(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'panel_t' THEN h.min_value END),
         MAX(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'panel_t' THEN h.max_value END)
  FROM agg_sensor_hour h
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = h.sensor_key
  JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = h.time_key
  WHERE (d.sat_key, t.day) IN (SELECT d2.sat_key, t2.day
                               FROM v_stg_accepted a
                               JOIN dim_sensor d2 ON d2.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
                               JOIN dim_time   t2 ON t2.time_key   = a.time_key
                               WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY d.sat_key, t.day;

  -- Passes: any pass that overlaps the stretch of time this batch covers
  -- may have gained or changed readings, including a pass that heard
  -- nothing at all. Passes outside the calendar wait for their data.
  INSERT OR REPLACE INTO fact_pass (pass_id, sat_key, station_key, time_key, planned_minutes,
                                    readings_heard, first_heard, last_heard)
  SELECT p.pass_id,
         ds.sat_key,
         st.station_key,
         t.time_key,
         (unixepoch(p.los) - unixepoch(p.aos)) / 60,
         COUNT(f.reading_id),
         MIN(f.ts),
         MAX(f.ts)
  FROM contact_pass p
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = p.sat_id
  JOIN dim_station   st ON st.station_id = p.station_id
  JOIN dim_time      t  ON t.hour_start = strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', p.aos)
  LEFT JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sat_key = ds.sat_key
  LEFT JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = d.sensor_key
                          AND f.ts >= p.aos
                          AND f.ts < p.los
  WHERE p.los > (SELECT MIN(ts) FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
    AND p.aos <= (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY p.pass_id;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT sensor_key, time_key
                                        FROM v_stg_accepted
                                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id))
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

CREATE VIEW v_sensor_hour AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       t.time_key,
       t.hour_start,
       a.n,
       a.min_value,
       a.max_value,
       ROUND(a.sum_value / a.n, 3) AS avg_value
FROM agg_sensor_hour a
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key;

-- A day is rolled up from its hours: total sum over total count. An
-- average of the hourly averages would weigh a half-empty hour like a full one.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_day AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       t.day,
       SUM(a.n) AS n,
       MIN(a.min_value) AS min_value,
       MAX(a.max_value) AS max_value,
       ROUND(SUM(a.sum_value) / SUM(a.n), 3) AS avg_value
FROM agg_sensor_hour a
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key
GROUP BY d.sat_code, d.type_code, t.day;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run the pipeline once for every batch in the landing zone, oldest first.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landing_packet
ORDER BY batch_id;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('staged', '1', 1382), ('staged', '2', 1322), ('staged', '3', 2706),
  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'quarantine') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT batch_id || ':' || reason AS item, packets AS actual
                 FROM v_quarantine_summary) a
  ON a.item = e.item

  ('facts', 'ORB-1', 1144), ('facts', 'ORB-2', 1137), ('facts', 'ORB-3', 1104),
  ('facts', 'ORB-4', 1148), ('facts', 'ORB-5', 846),
  ('dims', 'dim_satellite', 6), ('dims', 'dim_sensor', 23),

CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test IN ('facts', 'dims')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'facts' AS test, d.sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading f
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_code
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_satellite', COUNT(*) FROM dim_satellite
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_sensor',    COUNT(*) FROM dim_sensor
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_station',   COUNT(*) FROM dim_station
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_time',      COUNT(*) FROM dim_time) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE TABLE expect_correction (
  sat_code  TEXT NOT NULL,
  type_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  ts        TEXT NOT NULL,
  old_value REAL NOT NULL,
  new_value REAL NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_code, type_code, ts)
);

INSERT INTO expect_correction (sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value) VALUES
  ('ORB-1', 'batt_v', '2026-03-01 10:50:00', 28.4, 28.35);

CREATE VIEW test_lineage AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'lineage') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_corrections AS
SELECT 'missing' AS problem, sat_code, type_code, ts FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value FROM expect_correction
  EXCEPT
  SELECT d.sat_code, d.type_code, c.ts, c.old_value, c.new_value
  FROM fact_correction c JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'unexpected', sat_code, type_code, ts FROM (
  SELECT d.sat_code, d.type_code, c.ts, c.old_value, c.new_value
  FROM fact_correction c JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key
  EXCEPT
  SELECT sat_code, type_code, ts, old_value, new_value FROM expect_correction);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('day', 'ORB-1 2026-03-01', 576), ('day', 'ORB-1 2026-03-02', 568),
  ('day', 'ORB-2 2026-03-01', 577), ('day', 'ORB-2 2026-03-02', 560),
  ('day', 'ORB-3 2026-03-01', 528), ('day', 'ORB-3 2026-03-02', 576),
  ('day', 'ORB-4 2026-03-01', 576), ('day', 'ORB-4 2026-03-02', 572),
  ('day', 'ORB-5 2026-03-01', 426), ('day', 'ORB-5 2026-03-02', 420),
  ('pass_fact', 'planned', 30), ('pass_fact', 'lost', 5);

CREATE VIEW test_rollup AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('day', 'pass_fact')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT ds.sat_code || ' ' || a.day AS item, a.readings AS actual
                 FROM agg_satellite_day a
                 JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_key = a.sat_key
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'planned', COUNT(*) FROM fact_pass
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'lost', SUM(readings_heard = 0) FROM fact_pass) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
  UNION ALL SELECT 'lineage',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_lineage
  UNION ALL SELECT 'corrections',        COUNT(*)             FROM test_corrections
  UNION ALL SELECT 'rollup',             COUNT(*)             FROM test_rollup
);
--- hint
Both hourly statements use the same filter: `WHERE (sensor_key, time_key) IN (SELECT sensor_key, time_key FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)`. The insert reads `fact_reading` with that filter and groups by `sensor_key, time_key`.
--- hint
For the days, the touched cells are `SELECT d.sat_key, t.day FROM v_stg_accepted a JOIN dim_sensor d … JOIN dim_time t … WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id`, and the insert groups `agg_sensor_hour` joined to `dim_sensor` and `dim_time` by `d.sat_key, t.day`, with `MIN(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'batt_v' THEN h.min_value END)` and so on.
--- hint
For the passes: `FROM contact_pass p JOIN dim_satellite ds … JOIN dim_station st … JOIN dim_time t ON t.hour_start = strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', p.aos) LEFT JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sat_key = ds.sat_key LEFT JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = d.sensor_key AND f.ts >= p.aos AND f.ts < p.los`, grouped by `p.pass_id`, counting `f.reading_id`. `planned_minutes` is `(unixepoch(p.los) - unixepoch(p.aos)) / 60`.

+++ practice | An hourly rollup of antenna temperatures
--- schema
CREATE TABLE fact_temp (antenna TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, temp_c REAL NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (antenna, ts));
INSERT INTO fact_temp VALUES
  ('A1', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 12.0), ('A1', '2026-03-01 10:20:00', 13.0), ('A1', '2026-03-01 10:40:00', 14.5),
  ('A1', '2026-03-01 11:00:00', 15.0), ('A2', '2026-03-01 10:10:00', 9.0), ('A2', '2026-03-01 11:30:00', 8.0),
  ('A2', '2026-03-01 11:50:00', 7.5);
--- task
Readings are in `fact_temp (antenna, ts, temp_c)`. Create the table `agg_temp_hour (antenna, hour_start, n, min_c, max_c, sum_c)` with the primary key `(antenna, hour_start)`, where `hour_start` is the reading's hour as `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:00:00'`, and fill it from `fact_temp` with one `INSERT … SELECT`. Then create the view `temp_hour (antenna, hour_start, n, avg_c)` with `avg_c = ROUND(sum_c / n, 2)`.
--- starter
CREATE TABLE agg_temp_hour (
  antenna    TEXT NOT NULL,
  hour_start TEXT NOT NULL,
  n          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  min_c      REAL NOT NULL,
  max_c      REAL NOT NULL,
  sum_c      REAL NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (antenna, hour_start)
);
--- solution
CREATE TABLE agg_temp_hour (
  antenna    TEXT NOT NULL,
  hour_start TEXT NOT NULL,
  n          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  min_c      REAL NOT NULL,
  max_c      REAL NOT NULL,
  sum_c      REAL NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (antenna, hour_start)
);

INSERT INTO agg_temp_hour (antenna, hour_start, n, min_c, max_c, sum_c)
SELECT antenna, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts), COUNT(*), MIN(temp_c), MAX(temp_c), SUM(temp_c)
FROM fact_temp
GROUP BY antenna, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts);

CREATE VIEW temp_hour AS
SELECT antenna, hour_start, n, ROUND(sum_c / n, 2) AS avg_c
FROM agg_temp_hour;
--- hint
`strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts)` rounds a moment down to its hour. Group by the antenna and that expression.
--- hint
Store `COUNT(*)`, `MIN`, `MAX` and `SUM`; the view divides the sum by the count.
--- check query | Four antenna-hours
SELECT antenna, hour_start, n, min_c, max_c, sum_c FROM agg_temp_hour ORDER BY antenna, hour_start
=> [["A1", "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 3, 12.0, 14.5, 39.5], ["A1", "2026-03-01 11:00:00", 1, 15.0, 15.0, 15.0], ["A2", "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 1, 9.0, 9.0, 9.0], ["A2", "2026-03-01 11:00:00", 2, 7.5, 8.0, 15.5]]
--- check query | The view's averages
SELECT antenna, hour_start, avg_c FROM temp_hour ORDER BY antenna, hour_start
=> [["A1", "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 13.17], ["A1", "2026-03-01 11:00:00", 15.0], ["A2", "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 9.0], ["A2", "2026-03-01 11:00:00", 7.75]]
--- check query | Nothing is lost
SELECT SUM(n) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_temp) FROM agg_temp_hour
=> [[1]]

+++ practice | A day from its hours, the honest way
--- schema
CREATE TABLE agg_hour (sensor TEXT NOT NULL, hour_start TEXT NOT NULL, n INTEGER NOT NULL, sum_v REAL NOT NULL, avg_v REAL NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (sensor, hour_start));
INSERT INTO agg_hour VALUES
  ('S1', '2026-03-01 00:00:00', 6, 186.0, 31.0),
  ('S1', '2026-03-01 01:00:00', 2, 70.0, 35.0),
  ('S1', '2026-03-01 02:00:00', 6, 192.0, 32.0),
  ('S2', '2026-03-01 00:00:00', 1, 20.0, 20.0),
  ('S2', '2026-03-01 01:00:00', 5, 125.0, 25.0),
  ('S1', '2026-03-02 00:00:00', 6, 180.0, 30.0);
--- task
The hourly rollup `agg_hour (sensor, hour_start, n, sum_v, avg_v)` stores each hour's count, sum and average. This daily view averages the hourly averages, which weighs S1's two-reading hour like its full ones:

```sql
CREATE VIEW day_avg AS
SELECT sensor, date(hour_start) AS day, SUM(n) AS n, ROUND(AVG(avg_v), 3) AS avg_v
FROM agg_hour
GROUP BY sensor, date(hour_start);
```

Fix `day_avg`, keeping its columns, so `avg_v` is the true average of all the day's readings, rounded to 3 decimals.
--- starter
CREATE VIEW day_avg AS
SELECT sensor, date(hour_start) AS day, SUM(n) AS n, ROUND(AVG(avg_v), 3) AS avg_v
FROM agg_hour
GROUP BY sensor, date(hour_start);
--- solution
CREATE VIEW day_avg AS
SELECT sensor, date(hour_start) AS day, SUM(n) AS n, ROUND(SUM(sum_v) / SUM(n), 3) AS avg_v
FROM agg_hour
GROUP BY sensor, date(hour_start);
--- hint
The day's average is the day's total over the day's count. Both are sums of the hourly columns.
--- hint
`ROUND(SUM(sum_v) / SUM(n), 3)`.
--- check query | The true daily averages
SELECT sensor, day, n, avg_v FROM day_avg ORDER BY sensor, day
=> [["S1", "2026-03-01", 14, 32.0], ["S1", "2026-03-02", 6, 30.0], ["S2", "2026-03-01", 6, 24.167]]
--- check query | S1 on 1 March is 448 / 14, not the average of 31, 35 and 32
SELECT avg_v FROM day_avg WHERE sensor = 'S1' AND day = '2026-03-01'
=> [[32.0]]
--- check query | S2's day weighs its five-reading hour five times
SELECT avg_v FROM day_avg WHERE sensor = 'S2'
=> [[24.167]]

+++ practice | Recompute only what the batch touched
--- schema
CREATE TABLE fact (sensor TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (sensor, ts));
INSERT INTO fact VALUES
  ('S1', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 5.0, 1), ('S1', '2026-03-01 10:30:00', 7.0, 1),
  ('S1', '2026-03-01 11:00:00', 6.0, 1), ('S2', '2026-03-01 10:15:00', 3.0, 1);
CREATE TABLE agg (sensor TEXT NOT NULL, hour_start TEXT NOT NULL, n INTEGER NOT NULL, max_v REAL NOT NULL, sum_v REAL NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (sensor, hour_start));
INSERT INTO agg VALUES
  ('S1', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 2, 7.0, 12.0), ('S1', '2026-03-01 11:00:00', 1, 6.0, 6.0),
  ('S2', '2026-03-01 10:00:00', 1, 3.0, 3.0);
CREATE TABLE batch_rows (batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL, sensor TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE rollup_request (request_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL);
--- task
`fact (sensor, ts, value, batch_id)` holds the readings and `agg (sensor, hour_start, n, max_v, sum_v)` their hourly rollup. When a batch is loaded, the (sensor, ts) pairs it sent are listed in `batch_rows (batch_id, sensor, ts)`.

Create the trigger `rollup_batch`: after a row is inserted into `rollup_request`, recompute from `fact` the `agg` rows of every (sensor, hour) that the batch sent readings for: delete those rows, then insert them again. Leave every other `agg` row alone.
--- starter
CREATE TRIGGER rollup_batch AFTER INSERT ON rollup_request
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO agg (sensor, hour_start, n, max_v, sum_v)
  SELECT sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts), COUNT(*), MAX(value), SUM(value)
  FROM fact WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  GROUP BY sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts)
  ON CONFLICT (sensor, hour_start) DO UPDATE SET
    n = n + excluded.n, max_v = MAX(max_v, excluded.max_v), sum_v = sum_v + excluded.sum_v;
END;
--- solution
CREATE TRIGGER rollup_batch AFTER INSERT ON rollup_request
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM agg
  WHERE (sensor, hour_start) IN (SELECT sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts)
                                 FROM batch_rows WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id);
  INSERT INTO agg (sensor, hour_start, n, max_v, sum_v)
  SELECT sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts), COUNT(*), MAX(value), SUM(value)
  FROM fact
  WHERE (sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts)) IN
        (SELECT sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts) FROM batch_rows WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts);
END;
--- hint
Adding the batch's numbers to the old ones double-counts a rerun, and cannot take back a value that a correction replaced. Throw the touched cells away and compute them again from all the facts in them.
--- hint
Both statements filter on the pair: `WHERE (sensor, hour_start) IN (SELECT sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts) FROM batch_rows WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)`, and in the insert the left side is `(sensor, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', ts))`.
--- check query | Batch 2 corrects S1 at 10:30 and adds a reading at 10:45: the 10:00 cell is recomputed

INSERT INTO fact VALUES ('S1', '2026-03-01 10:45:00', 6.5, 2);
INSERT INTO batch_rows VALUES (2, 'S1', '2026-03-01 10:30:00'), (2, 'S1', '2026-03-01 10:45:00');
INSERT INTO rollup_request (batch_id) VALUES (2);
SELECT sensor, hour_start, n, max_v, sum_v FROM agg ORDER BY sensor, hour_start
=> [["S1", "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 3, 6.5, 15.5], ["S1", "2026-03-01 11:00:00", 1, 6.0, 6.0], ["S2", "2026-03-01 10:00:00", 1, 3.0, 3.0]]
--- check query | Running batch 2 again changes nothing

SELECT SUM(n), SUM(sum_v) FROM agg
=> [[5, 24.5]]
--- check query | The untouched cells are the same rows as before

=> [[1, 3.0]]

+++ practice | Satellite days side by side
--- schema
CREATE TABLE agg_hour (sat TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, day TEXT NOT NULL, hour INTEGER NOT NULL, n INTEGER NOT NULL, min_v REAL NOT NULL, max_v REAL NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO agg_hour VALUES
  ('ORB-1', 'batt_v', '2026-03-01', 0, 6, 26.8, 28.5), ('ORB-1', 'batt_v', '2026-03-01', 1, 6, 26.9, 28.4),
  ('ORB-1', 'cpu_t', '2026-03-01', 0, 6, 30.0, 33.5), ('ORB-1', 'cpu_t', '2026-03-01', 1, 5, 31.0, 34.0),
  ('ORB-2', 'batt_v', '2026-03-01', 0, 6, 27.0, 28.2), ('ORB-2', 'wheel_rpm', '2026-03-01', 0, 6, 1900, 2100),
  ('ORB-1', 'batt_v', '2026-03-02', 0, 4, 25.9, 28.0);
--- task
The hourly rollup `agg_hour (sat, kind, day, hour, n, min_v, max_v)` has one row per satellite, kind of sensor and hour. Create the view `sat_day (sat, day, readings, kinds, min_batt_v, max_cpu_t)` with one row per satellite and day:

- `readings`: the sum of `n`
- `kinds`: how many different kinds of sensor reported
- `min_batt_v`: the lowest battery (`batt_v`) reading of the day, or NULL when there was none
- `max_cpu_t`: the highest `cpu_t` reading of the day, or NULL when there was none
--- starter
CREATE VIEW sat_day AS
SELECT sat, day, SUM(n) AS readings, COUNT(*) AS kinds,
       MIN(min_v) AS min_batt_v, MAX(max_v) AS max_cpu_t
FROM agg_hour
GROUP BY sat, day;
--- solution
CREATE VIEW sat_day AS
SELECT sat,
       day,
       SUM(n) AS readings,
       COUNT(DISTINCT kind) AS kinds,
       MIN(CASE WHEN kind = 'batt_v' THEN min_v END) AS min_batt_v,
       MAX(CASE WHEN kind = 'cpu_t' THEN max_v END) AS max_cpu_t
FROM agg_hour
GROUP BY sat, day;
--- hint
`MIN(min_v)` takes the lowest value of every kind of sensor, wheel speeds included. A `CASE` inside the aggregate keeps only one kind: the other rows become NULL, and `MIN` and `MAX` skip NULLs.
--- hint
`kinds` counts different kinds, not rows: `COUNT(DISTINCT kind)`.
--- check query | Three satellite-days
SELECT sat, day, readings, kinds, min_batt_v, max_cpu_t FROM sat_day ORDER BY sat, day
=> [["ORB-1", "2026-03-01", 23, 2, 26.8, 34.0], ["ORB-1", "2026-03-02", 4, 1, 25.9, null], ["ORB-2", "2026-03-01", 12, 2, 27.0, null]]
--- check query | ORB-2 has no CPU readings, so its max_cpu_t is NULL, not a wheel speed

  (2, 'ORB-1', '2026-03-01 02:50:00', '2026-03-01 03:10:00'),

  ('ORB-1', '2026-03-01 03:00:00', 3.0), ('ORB-1', '2026-03-01 03:10:00', 4.0),
  ('ORB-2', '2026-03-01 01:10:00', 5.0), ('ORB-2', '2026-03-01 03:50:00', 6.0);
--- task
Planned contact windows are in `window_plan (win_id, sat, opens, closes)` and readings in `reading (sat, ts, value)`. A reading belongs to a window when it is from the same satellite and `opens <= ts < closes`.

Create the view `window_heard (win_id, sat, planned_minutes, heard, first_heard, last_heard)` with **one row per window**, including windows that heard nothing (`heard` 0, the times NULL). `planned_minutes` is the whole minutes from `opens` to `closes`.
--- starter
CREATE VIEW window_heard AS
SELECT w.win_id, w.sat, 12 AS planned_minutes, COUNT(*) AS heard, MIN(r.ts) AS first_heard, MAX(r.ts) AS last_heard
FROM window_plan w
JOIN reading r ON r.sat = w.sat AND r.ts BETWEEN w.opens AND w.closes
GROUP BY w.win_id;
--- solution
CREATE VIEW window_heard AS
SELECT w.win_id,
       w.sat,
       (unixepoch(w.closes) - unixepoch(w.opens)) / 60 AS planned_minutes,
       COUNT(r.ts) AS heard,
       MIN(r.ts) AS first_heard,
       MAX(r.ts) AS last_heard
FROM window_plan w
LEFT JOIN reading r ON r.sat = w.sat AND r.ts >= w.opens AND r.ts < w.closes
GROUP BY w.win_id;
--- hint
Three things: the silent window disappears with an inner `JOIN`; `BETWEEN` includes the closing moment, which does not belong to the window; and not every window is 12 minutes long.
--- hint
`LEFT JOIN reading r ON r.sat = w.sat AND r.ts >= w.opens AND r.ts < w.closes`, count `r.ts`, and compute the minutes with `(unixepoch(w.closes) - unixepoch(w.opens)) / 60`.
