-- The one place that turns packet codes into a sensor: which satellite
-- carries which kind of sensor, with the limits that make a value possible.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_catalog AS
SELECT se.sensor_id,
       sa.sat_id,
       sa.code   AS sat_code,
       sa.status AS sat_status,
       st.type_code,
       st.unit,
       st.min_valid,
       st.max_valid
FROM sensor se
JOIN satellite   sa ON sa.sat_id    = se.sat_id
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = se.type_code;

-- The roster the operations team reads every morning.
CREATE VIEW v_fleet_roster AS
SELECT sa.code AS sat_code,
       sa.name,
       sa.status,
       COUNT(se.sensor_id) AS sensors,
       COALESCE((SELECT group_concat(type_code, ',')
                 FROM (SELECT type_code FROM sensor
                       WHERE sat_id = sa.sat_id
                       ORDER BY type_code)), '') AS sensor_types,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact_pass p WHERE p.sat_id = sa.sat_id) AS passes
FROM satellite sa
LEFT JOIN sensor se ON se.sat_id = sa.sat_id
GROUP BY sa.sat_id
ORDER BY sa.code;

-- Thresholds the reports use, kept as data so operations can tune them
-- without touching a query.
CREATE TABLE ops_config (
  key   TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  value REAL NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO ops_config (key, value) VALUES
  ('cadence_minutes', 10),    -- every sensor reports every 10 minutes
  ('outage_minutes',  30),    -- a silence this long or longer is an outage
  ('low_battery_v',   26.5),  -- below this the battery is low
  ('min_streak',      3);     -- a low-battery streak needs this many readings

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1b. Audit trail. Every change to the operational tables is recorded,
--     each satellite's status history is kept with its dates, and a
--     status change is made by logging an operations event.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE audit_log (
  audit_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  table_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  row_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
  action     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('insert', 'update', 'delete')),
  old_row    TEXT CHECK (old_row IS NULL OR json_valid(old_row)),
  new_row    TEXT CHECK (new_row IS NULL OR json_valid(new_row))
);

-- One row per stretch of time a satellite spent in one status.
-- valid_to is NULL for the stretch that is still going on.
CREATE TABLE satellite_status_history (
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  status     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  valid_from TEXT    NOT NULL,
  valid_to   TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_id, valid_from),
  CHECK (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_from)
);

INSERT INTO satellite_status_history (sat_id, status, valid_from)
SELECT sat_id, status, status_since
FROM satellite;

-- What the operations team did, and why. Inserting an event is how a
-- satellite's status is changed.
CREATE TABLE ops_event (
  event_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  at         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (at IS datetime(at, '+0 seconds')),
  new_status TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (new_status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  note       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TRIGGER ops_event_apply AFTER INSERT ON ops_event
BEGIN
  UPDATE satellite
  SET status = NEW.new_status,
      status_since = NEW.at
  WHERE sat_id = NEW.sat_id;
END;

CREATE TRIGGER satellite_audit_insert AFTER INSERT ON satellite
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, row_key, action, old_row, new_row)
  VALUES ('satellite', NEW.code, 'insert', NULL,
          json_object('name', NEW.name, 'status', NEW.status, 'status_since', NEW.status_since));
  INSERT INTO satellite_status_history (sat_id, status, valid_from)
  VALUES (NEW.sat_id, NEW.status, NEW.status_since);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER satellite_audit_update AFTER UPDATE ON satellite
WHEN OLD.name IS NOT NEW.name
  OR OLD.status IS NOT NEW.status
  OR OLD.status_since IS NOT NEW.status_since
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, row_key, action, old_row, new_row)
  VALUES ('satellite', NEW.code, 'update',
          json_object('name', OLD.name, 'status', OLD.status, 'status_since', OLD.status_since),
          json_object('name', NEW.name, 'status', NEW.status, 'status_since', NEW.status_since));
END;

-- Close the stretch that was going on, open a new one, and keep the
-- warehouse's copy of the status in step.
CREATE TRIGGER satellite_status_change AFTER UPDATE OF status ON satellite
WHEN OLD.status IS NOT NEW.status
BEGIN
  UPDATE satellite_status_history
  SET valid_to = NEW.status_since
  WHERE sat_id = NEW.sat_id
    AND valid_to IS NULL;
  INSERT INTO satellite_status_history (sat_id, status, valid_from)
  VALUES (NEW.sat_id, NEW.status, NEW.status_since);
  UPDATE dim_satellite
  SET status = NEW.status
  WHERE sat_id = NEW.sat_id;
END;

CREATE TRIGGER sensor_type_audit_update AFTER UPDATE ON sensor_type
WHEN OLD.label IS NOT NEW.label
  OR OLD.unit IS NOT NEW.unit
  OR OLD.min_valid IS NOT NEW.min_valid
  OR OLD.max_valid IS NOT NEW.max_valid
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, row_key, action, old_row, new_row)
  VALUES ('sensor_type', NEW.type_code, 'update',
          json_object('unit', OLD.unit, 'min_valid', OLD.min_valid, 'max_valid', OLD.max_valid),
          json_object('unit', NEW.unit, 'min_valid', NEW.min_valid, 'max_valid', NEW.max_valid));
  UPDATE dim_sensor
  SET unit = NEW.unit,
      type_label = NEW.label
  WHERE type_code = NEW.type_code;
END;

CREATE TRIGGER sensor_audit_insert AFTER INSERT ON sensor
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, row_key, action, old_row, new_row)
  VALUES ('sensor', CAST(NEW.sensor_id AS TEXT), 'insert', NULL,
          json_object('sat_id', NEW.sat_id, 'type_code', NEW.type_code));
END;

CREATE TRIGGER sensor_audit_delete AFTER DELETE ON sensor
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, row_key, action, old_row, new_row)
  VALUES ('sensor', CAST(OLD.sensor_id AS TEXT), 'delete',
          json_object('sat_id', OLD.sat_id, 'type_code', OLD.type_code), NULL);
END;

-- A late-arriving dimension: packets from a sensor nobody had registered
-- yet were quarantined as unknown_sensor. Registering the sensor re-runs
-- every batch that holds one of them, so they load without anyone asking.
CREATE TRIGGER sensor_release_parked AFTER INSERT ON sensor
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
  SELECT DISTINCT st.batch_id
  FROM stg_reading st
  JOIN satellite s ON s.code = st.sat_code
  WHERE st.reject_reason = 'unknown_sensor'
    AND s.sat_id = NEW.sat_id
    AND st.type_code = NEW.type_code
  ORDER BY st.batch_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Pipeline control. SQLite has no stored procedures, so each step is
--    a trigger that fires when a row is added to etl_step. Running the
--    pipeline for a batch is one INSERT INTO etl_run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE etl_run (
  run_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE etl_step (
  step_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  step      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (step IN ('stage', 'validate', 'load', 'rollup', 'dq')),
  rows_in   INTEGER,
  rows_out  INTEGER
);

-- One run is its steps, in order. A multi-row INSERT fires the step
-- triggers row by row, so each step sees the work of the one before.
CREATE TRIGGER etl_run_steps AFTER INSERT ON etl_run
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO etl_step (run_id, batch_id, step) VALUES
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'stage'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'validate'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'load'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'rollup'),
    (NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, 'dq');
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Staging: one row per landed packet, parsed but not yet trusted.
--    No constraints on the parsed columns: staging must accept anything,
--    so that nothing that arrived is ever lost.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE stg_reading (
  batch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,              -- the packet exactly as it landed
  is_object     INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- 1 when body is a JSON object
  sat_code      TEXT,              -- trimmed, upper case
  type_code     TEXT,              -- trimmed, lower case
  ts_raw        TEXT,
  v_raw,                           -- no type on purpose: keeps 28.4 and '28.4' apart
  v_type        TEXT,              -- json_type of v: 'integer', 'real', 'text', ...
  -- filled in by the validate step
  ts            TEXT,              -- canonical 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', UTC
  sensor_id     INTEGER,           -- resolved through v_sensor_catalog
  value         REAL,
  reject_reason TEXT               -- NULL when the row passed every rule
);

-- Every pipeline step reads one batch of staging: find it without a scan.
CREATE INDEX idx_stg_batch ON stg_reading (batch_id);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_stage AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'stage'
BEGIN
  -- Idempotent: a rerun replaces the batch instead of adding to it.
  DELETE FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO stg_reading (batch_id, line_no, body, is_object,
                           sat_code, type_code, ts_raw, v_raw, v_type)
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         body,
         is_object,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN upper(trim(body ->> '$.sat')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN lower(trim(body ->> '$.sensor')) END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.ts' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN body ->> '$.v' END,
         CASE WHEN is_object THEN json_type(body, '$.v') END
  FROM (
    SELECT batch_id,
           line_no,
           body,
           -- json_type on text that is not JSON is an error, so test first
           CASE WHEN json_valid(body) THEN json_type(body) = 'object' ELSE 0 END AS is_object
    FROM landing_packet
    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  );

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading    WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Validation and quarantine. Every staged row either passes every
--    rule or is quarantined with exactly one reason: the first rule it
--    breaks, in the order the validate step checks them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE quarantine (
  batch_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  line_no   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason    TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN (
              'malformed_json', 'missing_field', 'bad_timestamp', 'non_numeric_value',
              'unknown_satellite', 'unknown_sensor', 'out_of_range')),
  body      TEXT,
  resolved  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resolved IN (0, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, line_no)
);

-- The triage screen only ever asks about open items: index just those.
CREATE INDEX idx_quarantine_open ON quarantine (reason, batch_id) WHERE resolved = 0;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_validate AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'validate'
BEGIN
  -- Pass 1: parse. Each column stays NULL when its raw value cannot be used.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  -- The round trip goes through '+0 seconds' so SQLite does the date
  -- arithmetic: without a modifier it lets a time like 24:30 through.
  SET ts        = CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ts_raw, '+0 seconds') = ts_raw
                       THEN datetime(ts_raw) END,
      value     = CASE WHEN v_type IN ('integer', 'real') THEN v_raw END,
      sensor_id = (SELECT c.sensor_id
                   FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                   WHERE c.sat_code  = stg_reading.sat_code
                     AND c.type_code = stg_reading.type_code)
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Pass 2: judge. The first rule broken is the reason; NULL means clean.
  UPDATE stg_reading
  SET reject_reason = CASE
        WHEN NOT is_object THEN 'malformed_json'
        WHEN sat_code IS NULL OR type_code IS NULL
          OR ts_raw IS NULL OR v_raw IS NULL THEN 'missing_field'
        WHEN ts IS NULL THEN 'bad_timestamp'
        WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'non_numeric_value'
        WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM satellite s WHERE s.code = stg_reading.sat_code)
          THEN 'unknown_satellite'
        WHEN sensor_id IS NULL THEN 'unknown_sensor'
        WHEN value < (SELECT c.min_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          OR value > (SELECT c.max_valid FROM v_sensor_catalog c
                      WHERE c.sensor_id = stg_reading.sensor_id)
          THEN 'out_of_range'
      END
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id;

  -- Quarantine the rejects. A rerun refreshes the reason but keeps the
  -- triage flag someone may already have set.
  DELETE FROM quarantine
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND line_no NOT IN (SELECT line_no
                        FROM stg_reading
                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
                          AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL);

  INSERT INTO quarantine (batch_id, line_no, reason, body)
  SELECT batch_id, line_no, reject_reason, body
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND reject_reason IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id, line_no) DO UPDATE SET
    reason = excluded.reason,
    body   = excluded.body;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- Rejects per batch and reason: the first thing to read after a load.
CREATE VIEW v_quarantine_summary AS
SELECT batch_id,
       reason,
       COUNT(*) AS packets
FROM quarantine
GROUP BY batch_id, reason;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. The star schema. Grain of the fact table: one reading of one
--    sensor at one moment. Dimensions use surrogate keys (sat_key,
--    sensor_key, time_key) so the warehouse does not depend on how the
--    operational tables number things.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE dim_satellite (
  sat_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: satellite.sat_id
  sat_code  TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  sat_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_sensor (
  sensor_key INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_id  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: sensor.sensor_id
  sat_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  sat_code   TEXT    NOT NULL,         -- copied in, so reports need no extra join
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  type_label TEXT    NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE dim_station (
  station_key  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- natural key: ground_station.station_id
  station_code TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  station_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  hemisphere   TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (hemisphere IN ('N', 'S'))  -- derived from latitude
);

-- A calendar, one row per hour, with no holes: an hour with no readings
-- still has a row, which is how reports can show it as empty.
CREATE TABLE dim_time (
  time_key   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                               -- YYYYMMDDHH
  hour_start TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,                           -- '2026-03-01 14:00:00'
  day        TEXT    NOT NULL,                                  -- '2026-03-01'
  hour       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (hour BETWEEN 0 AND 23),
  weekday    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Sunday
  shift      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (shift IN ('A', 'B', 'C'))  -- 00-08, 08-16, 16-24
);

CREATE TABLE fact_reading (
  reading_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  ts         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  value      REAL    NOT NULL,
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- lineage: the batch this version came from
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts)       -- the grain, enforced
);

-- Fleet-wide questions about a stretch of hours start from the calendar key.
CREATE INDEX idx_fact_time ON fact_reading (time_key);

-- Covering indexes: every column these queries need is in the index,
-- so the table itself is never read.
CREATE INDEX idx_fact_batch_keys   ON fact_reading (batch_id, sensor_key, time_key);
CREATE INDEX idx_fact_sensor_trend ON fact_reading (sensor_key, ts, value);

-- Facts are never deleted: a wrong value is fixed by loading a correction.
CREATE TRIGGER fact_reading_append_only BEFORE DELETE ON fact_reading
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'fact_reading is append-only: load a correction instead');
END;

-- Every time a newer batch changed a value that was already loaded.
CREATE TABLE fact_correction (
  correction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sensor_key    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  ts            TEXT    NOT NULL,
  old_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  new_value     REAL    NOT NULL,
  old_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  new_batch     INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (new_batch > old_batch),
  run_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id)
);

-- Which batches have been loaded, and how many times.
CREATE TABLE etl_batch (
  batch_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  first_run INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  last_run  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  runs      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (runs >= 1)
);

-- One row per run: what went into and came out of each step, side by side.
CREATE VIEW v_pipeline_monitor AS
SELECT r.run_id,
       r.batch_id,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'stage'    THEN s.rows_out END) AS staged,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_out END) AS clean,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'validate' THEN s.rows_in - s.rows_out END) AS rejected,
       MAX(CASE WHEN s.step = 'load'     THEN s.rows_out END) AS facts_owned,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_correction c WHERE c.run_id = r.run_id) AS corrections
FROM etl_run r
JOIN etl_step s ON s.run_id = r.run_id
GROUP BY r.run_id, r.batch_id;

-- The clean rows of every batch, one per sensor and moment: when a batch
-- holds the same reading twice, its last line wins.
CREATE VIEW v_stg_accepted AS
SELECT r.batch_id,
       r.line_no,
       d.sensor_key,
       CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', r.ts) AS INTEGER) AS time_key,
       r.ts,
       r.value
FROM (
  SELECT batch_id,
         line_no,
         sensor_id,
         ts,
         value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batch_id, sensor_id, ts
                            ORDER BY line_no DESC) AS copy_rank
  FROM stg_reading
  WHERE reject_reason IS NULL
) r
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_id = r.sensor_id
WHERE r.copy_rank = 1;

CREATE TRIGGER etl_load AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'load'
BEGIN
  -- Dimensions first: a fact may only point at rows that exist.
  INSERT INTO dim_satellite (sat_id, sat_code, sat_name, status)
  SELECT sat_id, code, name, status
  FROM satellite
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY sat_id
  ON CONFLICT (sat_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_code = excluded.sat_code,
    sat_name = excluded.sat_name,
    status   = excluded.status;

  INSERT INTO dim_sensor (sensor_id, sat_key, sat_code, type_code, type_label, unit)
  SELECT se.sensor_id, ds.sat_key, ds.sat_code, st.type_code, st.label, st.unit
  FROM sensor se
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = se.sat_id
  JOIN sensor_type   st ON st.type_code = se.type_code
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY se.sensor_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_id) DO UPDATE SET
    sat_key    = excluded.sat_key,
    sat_code   = excluded.sat_code,
    type_label = excluded.type_label,
    unit       = excluded.unit;

  INSERT INTO dim_station (station_id, station_code, station_name, hemisphere)
  SELECT station_id, code, name, CASE WHEN latitude >= 0 THEN 'N' ELSE 'S' END
  FROM ground_station
  WHERE true
  ORDER BY station_id
  ON CONFLICT (station_id) DO UPDATE SET
    station_code = excluded.station_code,
    station_name = excluded.station_name,
    hemisphere   = excluded.hemisphere;

  -- The calendar: every hour from the earliest to the latest known reading.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dim_time (time_key, hour_start, day, hour, weekday, shift)
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         h,
         date(h),
         CAST(strftime('%H', h) AS INTEGER),
         CAST(strftime('%w', h) AS INTEGER),
         CASE WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '08' THEN 'A'
              WHEN strftime('%H', h) < '16' THEN 'B'
              ELSE 'C' END
  FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hours (h) AS (
      SELECT MIN(first_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MIN(hour_start) AS first_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MIN(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL)
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datetime(h, '+1 hour') FROM hours
      WHERE h < (SELECT MAX(last_hour) FROM (
        SELECT MAX(hour_start) AS last_hour FROM dim_time
        UNION ALL
        SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', MAX(ts)) FROM stg_reading
        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL))
    )
    SELECT h FROM hours WHERE h IS NOT NULL
  );

  -- Log corrections before they are applied: a newer batch that brings a
  -- different value for a reading already loaded.
  INSERT INTO fact_correction (sensor_key, ts, old_value, new_value, old_batch, new_batch, run_id)
  SELECT f.sensor_key, f.ts, f.value, a.value, f.batch_id, a.batch_id, NEW.run_id
  FROM v_stg_accepted a
  JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = a.sensor_key AND f.ts = a.ts
  WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id
    AND a.batch_id > f.batch_id
    AND a.value <> f.value;

  -- Facts: the version from the newest batch wins, whatever order the
  -- batches are loaded in. Rerunning a batch changes nothing.
  INSERT INTO fact_reading (sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no)
  SELECT sensor_key, time_key, ts, value, batch_id, line_no
  FROM v_stg_accepted
  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id
  ON CONFLICT (sensor_key, ts) DO UPDATE SET
    value    = excluded.value,
    batch_id = excluded.batch_id,
    line_no  = excluded.line_no
  WHERE excluded.batch_id > fact_reading.batch_id;

  INSERT INTO etl_batch (batch_id, first_run, last_run, runs)
  VALUES (NEW.batch_id, NEW.run_id, NEW.run_id, 1)
  ON CONFLICT (batch_id) DO UPDATE SET
    last_run = excluded.last_run,
    runs     = runs + 1;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading
                  WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id AND reject_reason IS NULL),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6. Rollups, kept up to date one batch at a time. Sums and counts are
--    stored, not averages, so a rollup can be rolled up again.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE agg_sensor_hour (
  sensor_key INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_sensor (sensor_key),
  time_key   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),
  n          INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (n > 0),
  min_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  max_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  sum_value  REAL    NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sensor_key, time_key)
);

-- One row per satellite and day, rolled up from the hours: the health
-- numbers the morning report needs, side by side.
CREATE TABLE agg_satellite_day (
  sat_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  day         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  readings    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (readings > 0),
  sensors     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  min_batt_v  REAL,
  max_cpu_t   REAL,
  min_panel_t REAL,
  max_panel_t REAL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sat_key, day)
);

-- A second fact table on the same dimensions. Grain: one planned pass.
-- It records what the station actually heard while the satellite was
-- overhead; readings_heard = 0 is a lost pass.
CREATE TABLE fact_pass (
  pass_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,  -- degenerate key: contact_pass.pass_id
  sat_key         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_satellite (sat_key),
  station_key     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_station (station_key),
  time_key        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_time (time_key),  -- hour of aos
  planned_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (planned_minutes > 0),
  readings_heard  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (readings_heard >= 0),
  first_heard     TEXT,
  last_heard      TEXT
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_rollup AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'rollup'
BEGIN
  -- Recompute only the hours this batch touched, from the facts, so a
  -- late or corrected reading lands in the right hour and a rerun is harmless.
  DELETE FROM agg_sensor_hour
  WHERE (sensor_key, time_key) IN (SELECT sensor_key, time_key
                                   FROM v_stg_accepted
                                   WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id);

  INSERT INTO agg_sensor_hour (sensor_key, time_key, n, min_value, max_value, sum_value)
  SELECT sensor_key,
         time_key,
         COUNT(*),
         MIN(value),
         MAX(value),
         SUM(value)
  FROM fact_reading
  WHERE (sensor_key, time_key) IN (SELECT sensor_key, time_key
                                   FROM v_stg_accepted
                                   WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY sensor_key, time_key;

  -- Then the days those hours belong to, from the hours.
  DELETE FROM agg_satellite_day
  WHERE (sat_key, day) IN (SELECT d.sat_key, t.day
                           FROM v_stg_accepted a
                           JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
                           JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key
                           WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id);

  INSERT INTO agg_satellite_day (sat_key, day, readings, sensors,
                                 min_batt_v, max_cpu_t, min_panel_t, max_panel_t)
  SELECT d.sat_key,
         t.day,
         SUM(h.n),
         COUNT(DISTINCT h.sensor_key),
         MIN(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'batt_v'  THEN h.min_value END),
         MAX(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'cpu_t'   THEN h.max_value END),
         MIN(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'panel_t' THEN h.min_value END),
         MAX(CASE WHEN d.type_code = 'panel_t' THEN h.max_value END)
  FROM agg_sensor_hour h
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = h.sensor_key
  JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = h.time_key
  WHERE (d.sat_key, t.day) IN (SELECT d2.sat_key, t2.day
                               FROM v_stg_accepted a
                               JOIN dim_sensor d2 ON d2.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
                               JOIN dim_time   t2 ON t2.time_key   = a.time_key
                               WHERE a.batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY d.sat_key, t.day;

  -- Passes: any pass that overlaps the stretch of time this batch covers
  -- may have gained or changed readings, including a pass that heard
  -- nothing at all. Passes outside the calendar wait for their data.
  INSERT OR REPLACE INTO fact_pass (pass_id, sat_key, station_key, time_key, planned_minutes,
                                    readings_heard, first_heard, last_heard)
  SELECT p.pass_id,
         ds.sat_key,
         st.station_key,
         t.time_key,
         (unixepoch(p.los) - unixepoch(p.aos)) / 60,
         COUNT(f.reading_id),
         MIN(f.ts),
         MAX(f.ts)
  FROM contact_pass p
  JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_id = p.sat_id
  JOIN dim_station   st ON st.station_id = p.station_id
  JOIN dim_time      t  ON t.hour_start = strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00', p.aos)
  LEFT JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sat_key = ds.sat_key
  LEFT JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = d.sensor_key
                          AND f.ts >= p.aos
                          AND f.ts < p.los
  WHERE p.los > (SELECT MIN(ts) FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
    AND p.aos <= (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id)
  GROUP BY p.pass_id;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_stg_accepted WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT sensor_key, time_key
                                        FROM v_stg_accepted
                                        WHERE batch_id = NEW.batch_id))
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

CREATE VIEW v_sensor_hour AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       t.time_key,
       t.hour_start,
       a.n,
       a.min_value,
       a.max_value,
       ROUND(a.sum_value / a.n, 3) AS avg_value
FROM agg_sensor_hour a
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key;

-- A day is rolled up from its hours: total sum over total count. An
-- average of the hourly averages would weigh a half-empty hour like a full one.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_day AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       t.day,
       SUM(a.n) AS n,
       MIN(a.min_value) AS min_value,
       MAX(a.max_value) AS max_value,
       ROUND(SUM(a.sum_value) / SUM(a.n), 3) AS avg_value
FROM agg_sensor_hour a
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key
GROUP BY d.sat_code, d.type_code, t.day;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 7. Trend reports with window functions.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Each reading with the average of the last hour of readings (a frame
-- measured in seconds, so a gap in the data shrinks it instead of
-- reaching back hours) and the change since the reading before. The
-- change is only a step when the reading before was exactly one cadence
-- earlier: across an outage it would compare two different orbits.
CREATE VIEW v_reading_trend AS
SELECT sat_code,
       type_code,
       sensor_key,
       ts,
       value,
       avg_1h,
       n_1h,
       CASE WHEN unixepoch(ts) - unixepoch(prev_ts) = 600
            THEN ROUND(value - prev_value, 3) END AS step
FROM (
  SELECT d.sat_code,
         d.type_code,
         f.sensor_key,
         f.ts,
         f.value,
         ROUND(AVG(f.value) OVER last_hour, 3) AS avg_1h,
         COUNT(*) OVER last_hour AS n_1h,
         LAG(f.ts)    OVER by_time AS prev_ts,
         LAG(f.value) OVER by_time AS prev_value
  FROM fact_reading f
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
  WINDOW last_hour AS (PARTITION BY f.sensor_key
                       ORDER BY unixepoch(f.ts)
                       RANGE BETWEEN 3000 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),
         by_time   AS (PARTITION BY f.sensor_key ORDER BY f.ts)
);

-- Each day, the satellites ranked by the peak of each kind of sensor.
CREATE VIEW v_daily_peak_rank AS
SELECT day,
       type_code,
       sat_code,
       peak,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY day, type_code ORDER BY peak DESC) AS peak_rank
FROM (
  SELECT t.day,
         d.type_code,
         d.sat_code,
         MAX(a.max_value) AS peak
  FROM agg_sensor_hour a
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
  JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = a.time_key
  GROUP BY t.day, d.type_code, d.sat_code
);

-- The three biggest jumps between consecutive readings, per kind of sensor.
CREATE VIEW v_top_steps AS
SELECT type_code,
       sat_code,
       ts,
       value,
       step,
       step_rank
FROM (
  SELECT type_code,
         sat_code,
         ts,
         value,
         step,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY type_code
                            ORDER BY abs(step) DESC, ts, sat_code) AS step_rank
  FROM v_reading_trend
  WHERE step IS NOT NULL
)
WHERE step_rank <= 3;

-- A reading far from its recent past: more than three standard
-- deviations from the mean of the 12 readings before it. Squares on both
-- sides, so no square root is needed:
--   (value - mean)^2 > 9 * variance,  variance = mean(x^2) - mean(x)^2
CREATE VIEW v_anomaly AS
SELECT sat_code,
       type_code,
       ts,
       value,
       ROUND(mean_before, 3) AS mean_before
FROM (
  SELECT d.sat_code,
         d.type_code,
         f.ts,
         f.value,
         AVG(f.value) OVER before_12 AS mean_before,
         AVG(f.value * f.value) OVER before_12 AS mean_square_before,
         COUNT(*) OVER before_12 AS n_before
  FROM fact_reading f
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
  WINDOW before_12 AS (PARTITION BY f.sensor_key
                       ORDER BY f.ts
                       ROWS BETWEEN 12 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING)
)
WHERE n_before = 12
  AND (value - mean_before) * (value - mean_before)
      > 9 * (mean_square_before - mean_before * mean_before);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 8. Gaps and islands: when did we lose a satellite, which hours are
--    empty, and when did a battery stay low?
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Every moment we heard from each satellite, from any of its sensors.
CREATE VIEW v_contact AS
SELECT DISTINCT
       d.sat_code,
       f.ts
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key;

-- Gaps: a silence of outage_minutes or more between two contacts.
CREATE VIEW v_outage AS
SELECT sat_code,
       prev_ts AS last_heard,
       ts      AS heard_again,
       gap_minutes,
       CAST(gap_minutes / (SELECT value FROM ops_config WHERE key = 'cadence_minutes')
            AS INTEGER) - 1 AS missed_readings
FROM (
  SELECT sat_code,
         ts,
         prev_ts,
         (unixepoch(ts) - unixepoch(prev_ts)) / 60 AS gap_minutes
  FROM (
    SELECT sat_code,
           ts,
           LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY sat_code ORDER BY ts) AS prev_ts
    FROM v_contact
  )
  WHERE prev_ts IS NOT NULL
)
WHERE gap_minutes >= (SELECT value FROM ops_config WHERE key = 'outage_minutes');

-- Islands of contact, the other way round: a new session starts at the
-- first contact and after every outage. A running count of the outages
-- so far numbers the sessions, so each session is one group.
CREATE VIEW v_contact_session AS
SELECT sat_code,
       session_no,
       MIN(ts)  AS started,
       MAX(ts)  AS ended,
       COUNT(*) AS contacts
FROM (
  SELECT sat_code,
         ts,
         1 + SUM(starts_session) OVER (PARTITION BY sat_code ORDER BY ts
                                       ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
           AS session_no
  FROM (
    SELECT sat_code,
           ts,
           CASE WHEN (unixepoch(ts) - unixepoch(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY sat_code ORDER BY ts))) / 60
                     >= (SELECT value FROM ops_config WHERE key = 'outage_minutes')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts_session
    FROM v_contact
  )
)
GROUP BY sat_code, session_no;

-- Gaps at the grain of an hour: every sensor of every satellite that is
-- not retired, for every hour of the calendar, with its reading count.
-- An hour the sensor was silent is a row with 0, not a missing row.
CREATE VIEW v_sensor_hour_grid AS
SELECT d.sensor_key,
       d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       t.time_key,
       t.hour_start,
       COALESCE(a.n, 0) AS n
FROM dim_sensor d
JOIN dim_satellite s ON s.sat_key = d.sat_key AND s.status <> 'retired'
CROSS JOIN dim_time t
LEFT JOIN agg_sensor_hour a ON a.sensor_key = d.sensor_key AND a.time_key = t.time_key;

-- Islands: runs of consecutive low battery readings. Inside a run the
-- slot number and the row number both go up by one, so their difference
-- is the same for the whole run; a missing reading ends the run.
CREATE VIEW v_low_battery_streak AS
SELECT sat_code,
       MIN(ts)    AS started,
       MAX(ts)    AS ended,
       COUNT(*)   AS readings,
       MIN(value) AS lowest
FROM (
  SELECT d.sat_code,
         f.ts,
         f.value,
         unixepoch(f.ts) / (60 * CAST((SELECT value FROM ops_config
                                       WHERE key = 'cadence_minutes') AS INTEGER))
           - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY f.sensor_key ORDER BY f.ts) AS island
  FROM fact_reading f
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
  WHERE d.type_code = 'batt_v'
    AND f.value < (SELECT value FROM ops_config WHERE key = 'low_battery_v')
)
GROUP BY sat_code, island
HAVING COUNT(*) >= (SELECT value FROM ops_config WHERE key = 'min_streak');

-- The latest reading of every sensor: the dashboard's first tile. The
-- UNIQUE (sensor_key, ts) index answers it without touching the table.
CREATE VIEW v_latest_reading AS
SELECT sensor_key,
       MAX(ts) AS last_ts
FROM fact_reading
GROUP BY sensor_key;

-- Each reading with the status its satellite was in at that moment.
CREATE VIEW v_reading_status AS
SELECT f.reading_id,
       d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       f.ts,
       f.value,
       h.status
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN dim_sensor    d  ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_key   = d.sat_key
JOIN satellite_status_history h
  ON h.sat_id = ds.sat_id
 AND f.ts >= h.valid_from
 AND (h.valid_to IS NULL OR f.ts < h.valid_to);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 9. Data quality. Each dq_ view lists the rows that break one rule, so
--    a healthy warehouse returns zero rows from every one of them.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Every landed packet is staged, and every staged row is either clean
-- or quarantined.
CREATE VIEW dq_batch_reconcile AS
SELECT l.batch_id,
       l.landed,
       s.staged,
       s.clean,
       q.quarantined
FROM (SELECT batch_id, COUNT(*) AS landed
      FROM landing_packet GROUP BY batch_id) l
LEFT JOIN (SELECT batch_id, COUNT(*) AS staged, SUM(reject_reason IS NULL) AS clean
           FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) s ON s.batch_id = l.batch_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT batch_id, COUNT(*) AS quarantined
           FROM quarantine GROUP BY batch_id) q ON q.batch_id = l.batch_id
WHERE l.batch_id IN (SELECT batch_id FROM etl_batch)
  AND (s.staged IS NOT l.landed
       OR COALESCE(s.clean, 0) + COALESCE(q.quarantined, 0) <> l.landed);

-- Staged rejects and quarantine must be the same set of packets.
CREATE VIEW dq_quarantine_mismatch AS
SELECT s.batch_id,
       s.line_no,
       s.reject_reason,
       q.reason
FROM stg_reading s
LEFT JOIN quarantine q ON q.batch_id = s.batch_id AND q.line_no = s.line_no
WHERE s.reject_reason IS NOT q.reason;

-- Facts whose keys point at nothing.
CREATE VIEW dq_fact_orphans AS
SELECT f.reading_id,
       f.sensor_key,
       f.time_key
FROM fact_reading f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dim_sensor d WHERE d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key)
   OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dim_time   t WHERE t.time_key   = f.time_key);

-- Facts filed under the wrong hour of the calendar.
CREATE VIEW dq_fact_time_key AS
SELECT reading_id,
       ts,
       time_key
FROM fact_reading
WHERE time_key <> CAST(strftime('%Y%m%d%H', ts) AS INTEGER);

-- Facts outside the limits their sensor type allows today.
CREATE VIEW dq_fact_out_of_range AS
SELECT f.reading_id,
       d.type_code,
       f.value
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN dim_sensor  d  ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
JOIN sensor_type st ON st.type_code = d.type_code
WHERE f.value < st.min_valid OR f.value > st.max_valid;

-- A reading cannot be taken after the ground received its batch.
CREATE VIEW dq_future_readings AS
SELECT f.reading_id,
       f.ts,
       l.received_at
FROM fact_reading f
JOIN landing_packet l ON l.batch_id = f.batch_id AND l.line_no = f.line_no
WHERE f.ts > l.received_at;

-- Hourly rollups that no longer match the facts, in either direction.
CREATE VIEW dq_rollup_drift AS
SELECT COALESCE(a.sensor_key, r.sensor_key) AS sensor_key,
       COALESCE(a.time_key, r.time_key)     AS time_key,
       a.n AS rollup_n,
       r.n AS fact_n
FROM agg_sensor_hour a
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT sensor_key, time_key, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(value) AS min_value,
                        MAX(value) AS max_value, SUM(value) AS sum_value
                 FROM fact_reading
                 GROUP BY sensor_key, time_key) r
  ON r.sensor_key = a.sensor_key AND r.time_key = a.time_key
WHERE a.n IS NOT r.n
   OR a.min_value IS NOT r.min_value
   OR a.max_value IS NOT r.max_value
   OR abs(a.sum_value - r.sum_value) > 1e-6;

-- Daily rollups that no longer match the hours they come from.
CREATE VIEW dq_day_drift AS
SELECT COALESCE(a.sat_key, r.sat_key) AS sat_key,
       COALESCE(a.day, r.day)         AS day,
       a.readings AS rollup_readings,
       r.readings AS hour_readings
FROM agg_satellite_day a
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT d.sat_key, t.day, SUM(h.n) AS readings
                 FROM agg_sensor_hour h
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = h.sensor_key
                 JOIN dim_time   t ON t.time_key   = h.time_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_key, t.day) r
  ON r.sat_key = a.sat_key AND r.day = a.day
WHERE a.readings IS NOT r.readings;

-- Hours missing from the calendar between its first and last hour.
CREATE VIEW dq_calendar_gaps AS
SELECT hour_start AS before_gap,
       next_start AS after_gap
FROM (SELECT hour_start,
             LEAD(hour_start) OVER (ORDER BY hour_start) AS next_start
      FROM dim_time)
WHERE next_start IS NOT NULL
  AND next_start <> datetime(hour_start, '+1 hour');

-- The warehouse's copy of a sensor must agree with the operational tables.
CREATE VIEW dq_dim_sensor_drift AS
SELECT d.sensor_key,
       d.sensor_id,
       d.sat_code,
       d.unit
FROM dim_sensor d
LEFT JOIN v_sensor_catalog c ON c.sensor_id = d.sensor_id
WHERE c.sensor_id IS NULL
   OR c.sat_code  IS NOT d.sat_code
   OR c.type_code IS NOT d.type_code
   OR c.unit      IS NOT d.unit;

-- A station can track one satellite at a time.
CREATE VIEW dq_pass_overlap AS
SELECT a.pass_id AS pass_a,
       b.pass_id AS pass_b,
       a.station_id
FROM contact_pass a
JOIN contact_pass b
  ON b.station_id = a.station_id
 AND b.pass_id > a.pass_id
 AND b.aos < a.los
 AND a.aos < b.los;

-- Each satellite has exactly one stretch of status still going on, and
-- its stretches never overlap.
CREATE VIEW dq_status_history AS
SELECT sat_id,
       'open stretches: ' || COUNT(*) AS problem
FROM satellite_status_history
WHERE valid_to IS NULL
GROUP BY sat_id
HAVING COUNT(*) <> 1
UNION ALL
SELECT a.sat_id,
       'overlap at ' || b.valid_from
FROM satellite_status_history a
JOIN satellite_status_history b
  ON b.sat_id = a.sat_id
 AND b.valid_from > a.valid_from
 AND (a.valid_to IS NULL OR b.valid_from < a.valid_to);

-- The pass fact must agree with the readings it summarises.
CREATE VIEW dq_pass_drift AS
SELECT fp.pass_id,
       fp.readings_heard,
       COUNT(f.reading_id) AS recount
FROM fact_pass fp
JOIN contact_pass p ON p.pass_id = fp.pass_id
LEFT JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sat_key = fp.sat_key
LEFT JOIN fact_reading f ON f.sensor_key = d.sensor_key
                        AND f.ts >= p.aos
                        AND f.ts < p.los
GROUP BY fp.pass_id, fp.readings_heard
HAVING COUNT(f.reading_id) <> fp.readings_heard;

-- Sensors of satellites that are not retired which have said nothing in
-- the last three hours of the calendar: dead, or their packets are
-- being rejected.
CREATE VIEW dq_stale_sensors AS
SELECT d.sensor_key,
       d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       l.last_ts
FROM dim_sensor d
JOIN dim_satellite s ON s.sat_key = d.sat_key AND s.status <> 'retired'
LEFT JOIN v_latest_reading l ON l.sensor_key = d.sensor_key
WHERE l.last_ts IS NULL
   OR l.last_ts < datetime((SELECT MAX(hour_start) FROM dim_time), '-2 hours');


-- The data catalog: what every column an analyst can query means.
-- dq_undocumented keeps it honest when a table gains a column.
CREATE TABLE catalog_column (
  table_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  column_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  meaning     TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (table_name, column_name)
);

  ('dim_satellite', 'sat_key',         'Surrogate key of the satellite'),

  ('dim_satellite', 'sat_name',        'The satellite''s name'),
  ('dim_satellite', 'status',          'Current status: active, safe_mode or retired'),
  ('dim_sensor',    'sensor_key',      'Surrogate key of the sensor'),
  ('dim_sensor',    'sensor_id',       'Natural key: sensor.sensor_id'),

  ('dim_sensor',    'type_code',       'Kind of sensor, such as batt_v'),
  ('dim_sensor',    'type_label',      'Kind of sensor, in words'),
  ('dim_sensor',    'unit',            'Unit of every value the sensor reports'),
  ('dim_station',   'station_key',     'Surrogate key of the ground station'),
  ('dim_station',   'station_id',      'Natural key: ground_station.station_id'),
  ('dim_station',   'station_code',    'Three-letter station code'),

  ('dim_time',      'weekday',         'Day of the week, 0 = Sunday'),

  ('fact_reading',  'reading_id',      'Row id of the reading'),
  ('fact_reading',  'sensor_key',      'The sensor that took the reading'),
  ('fact_reading',  'time_key',        'The hour the reading falls in'),

  ('fact_pass',     'last_heard',      'Last reading during the pass'),
  ('fact_correction', 'correction_id', 'Row id of the correction'),
  ('fact_correction', 'sensor_key',    'The sensor whose reading changed'),
  ('fact_correction', 'ts',            'Moment of the reading that changed'),
  ('fact_correction', 'old_value',     'Value before the correction'),
  ('fact_correction', 'new_value',     'Value after the correction'),
  ('fact_correction', 'old_batch',     'Batch the old value came from'),
  ('fact_correction', 'new_batch',     'Batch that brought the new value'),
  ('fact_correction', 'run_id',        'Pipeline run that applied it'),
  ('agg_sensor_hour', 'sensor_key',    'The sensor'),
  ('agg_sensor_hour', 'time_key',      'The hour'),

  ('agg_sensor_hour', 'max_value',     'Highest reading in the hour'),

-- Columns an analyst can query that the catalog does not explain.
CREATE VIEW dq_undocumented AS
SELECT m.name AS table_name,
       c.name AS column_name
FROM sqlite_master m
JOIN pragma_table_info(m.name) c
WHERE m.type = 'table'
  AND (m.name GLOB 'dim_*' OR m.name GLOB 'fact_*' OR m.name GLOB 'agg_*'
       OR m.name = 'quarantine')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM catalog_column k
                  WHERE k.table_name = m.name AND k.column_name = c.name);

CREATE VIEW dq_summary AS
SELECT 'batch_reconcile'     AS check_name, COUNT(*) AS violations FROM dq_batch_reconcile
UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine_mismatch', COUNT(*) FROM dq_quarantine_mismatch
UNION ALL SELECT 'fact_orphans',        COUNT(*) FROM dq_fact_orphans
UNION ALL SELECT 'fact_time_key',       COUNT(*) FROM dq_fact_time_key
UNION ALL SELECT 'fact_out_of_range',   COUNT(*) FROM dq_fact_out_of_range
UNION ALL SELECT 'future_readings',     COUNT(*) FROM dq_future_readings
UNION ALL SELECT 'rollup_drift',        COUNT(*) FROM dq_rollup_drift
UNION ALL SELECT 'day_drift',           COUNT(*) FROM dq_day_drift
UNION ALL SELECT 'calendar_gaps',       COUNT(*) FROM dq_calendar_gaps
UNION ALL SELECT 'dim_sensor_drift',    COUNT(*) FROM dq_dim_sensor_drift
UNION ALL SELECT 'pass_overlap',        COUNT(*) FROM dq_pass_overlap
UNION ALL SELECT 'status_history',      COUNT(*) FROM dq_status_history
UNION ALL SELECT 'pass_drift',          COUNT(*) FROM dq_pass_drift
UNION ALL SELECT 'stale_sensors',       COUNT(*) FROM dq_stale_sensors
UNION ALL SELECT 'undocumented',        COUNT(*) FROM dq_undocumented;

-- The last step of every run records the checks, so a bad load is
-- visible in the log even if nobody looks at it that day.
CREATE TABLE dq_result (
  run_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES etl_run (run_id),
  batch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  check_name TEXT    NOT NULL,
  violations INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (violations >= 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, check_name)
);

CREATE TRIGGER etl_dq AFTER INSERT ON etl_step
WHEN NEW.step = 'dq'
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO dq_result (run_id, batch_id, check_name, violations)
  SELECT NEW.run_id, NEW.batch_id, check_name, violations
  FROM dq_summary;

  UPDATE etl_step
  SET rows_in  = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dq_summary),
      rows_out = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dq_summary WHERE violations > 0)
  WHERE step_id = NEW.step_id;
END;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 10. The report suite: what operations reads every morning. Each report
--     reads rollups or small views, never a full pass over the facts,
--     except the anomaly digest, which needs the readings themselves.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Per satellite and day: how complete the data is, and the extremes.
CREATE VIEW rpt_fleet_daily AS
SELECT ds.sat_code,
       a.day,
       a.readings,
       a.sensors * 144 AS expected,
       ROUND(100.0 * a.readings / (a.sensors * 144), 1) AS coverage_pct,
       a.min_batt_v,
       a.max_cpu_t,
       a.max_panel_t - a.min_panel_t AS panel_swing
FROM agg_satellite_day a
JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_key = a.sat_key;

-- Every outage, with the status the satellite was in when it went quiet.
CREATE VIEW rpt_outage_log AS
SELECT o.sat_code,
       o.last_heard,
       o.heard_again,
       o.gap_minutes,
       o.missed_readings,
       h.status AS status_when_lost
FROM v_outage o
JOIN satellite s ON s.code = o.sat_code
JOIN satellite_status_history h
  ON h.sat_id = s.sat_id
 AND o.last_heard >= h.valid_from
 AND (h.valid_to IS NULL OR o.last_heard < h.valid_to);

-- Planned passes when the station heard nothing, and the outage that
-- explains each one, if there is one.
CREATE VIEW rpt_lost_passes AS
SELECT fp.pass_id,
       ds.sat_code,
       st.station_code AS station,
       p.aos,
       p.los,
       o.gap_minutes AS outage_minutes
FROM fact_pass fp
JOIN contact_pass  p  ON p.pass_id = fp.pass_id
JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_key = fp.sat_key
JOIN dim_station   st ON st.station_key = fp.station_key
LEFT JOIN v_outage o  ON o.sat_code = ds.sat_code
                     AND p.aos < o.heard_again
                     AND o.last_heard < p.los
WHERE fp.readings_heard = 0;

-- Per station and day: passes planned, passes lost, readings heard.
CREATE VIEW rpt_station_daily AS
SELECT st.station_code AS station,
       t.day,
       COUNT(*) AS passes,
       SUM(fp.readings_heard = 0) AS lost,
       SUM(fp.readings_heard) AS readings_heard
FROM fact_pass fp
JOIN dim_station st ON st.station_key = fp.station_key
JOIN dim_time    t  ON t.time_key = fp.time_key
GROUP BY st.station_code, t.day;

-- Per batch: what arrived, what was rejected, what was loaded.
CREATE VIEW rpt_pipeline_batches AS
SELECT b.batch_id,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM landing_packet l WHERE l.batch_id = b.batch_id) AS landed,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM quarantine q WHERE q.batch_id = b.batch_id) AS rejected,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stg_reading s
        WHERE s.batch_id = b.batch_id AND s.reject_reason IS NULL) AS clean,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_stg_accepted a WHERE a.batch_id = b.batch_id) AS distinct_clean,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_reading f WHERE f.batch_id = b.batch_id) AS facts_owned,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_correction c WHERE c.new_batch = b.batch_id) AS corrections,
       b.runs
FROM etl_batch b;

-- The triage queue: open quarantine items per reason, oldest batch first.
CREATE VIEW rpt_quarantine_open AS
SELECT reason,
       COUNT(*) AS open_items,
       MIN(batch_id) AS oldest_batch
FROM quarantine
WHERE resolved = 0
GROUP BY reason;

-- The open items themselves, with what could be read from each packet,
-- so the person triaging sees the problem without parsing JSON by eye.
CREATE VIEW rpt_quarantine_detail AS
SELECT q.batch_id,
       q.line_no,
       q.reason,
       s.sat_code,
       s.type_code,
       s.ts_raw,
       s.v_raw,
       q.body
FROM quarantine q
LEFT JOIN stg_reading s ON s.batch_id = q.batch_id AND s.line_no = q.line_no
WHERE q.resolved = 0;

-- Every correction, readable: which sensor, what changed, by how much.
CREATE VIEW rpt_corrections AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       d.type_code,
       c.ts,
       c.old_value,
       c.new_value,
       ROUND(c.new_value - c.old_value, 3) AS delta,
       c.old_batch,
       c.new_batch
FROM fact_correction c
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = c.sensor_key;

-- Shift workload: readings per operations shift and day.
CREATE VIEW rpt_shift_load AS
SELECT t.day,
       t.shift,
       SUM(a.n) AS readings,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.time_key) AS hours_with_data
FROM agg_sensor_hour a
JOIN dim_time t ON t.time_key = a.time_key
GROUP BY t.day, t.shift;

-- Readings per hour, one column per satellite: the heat map on the
-- operations wall. A dip in a column is an outage.
CREATE VIEW rpt_hourly_heatmap AS
SELECT t.hour_start,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.sat_code = 'ORB-1' THEN a.n ELSE 0 END) AS orb_1,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.sat_code = 'ORB-2' THEN a.n ELSE 0 END) AS orb_2,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.sat_code = 'ORB-3' THEN a.n ELSE 0 END) AS orb_3,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.sat_code = 'ORB-4' THEN a.n ELSE 0 END) AS orb_4,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.sat_code = 'ORB-5' THEN a.n ELSE 0 END) AS orb_5
FROM dim_time t
LEFT JOIN agg_sensor_hour a ON a.time_key = t.time_key
LEFT JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = a.sensor_key
GROUP BY t.hour_start;

-- Battery health per satellite: the daily low and the low streaks.
CREATE VIEW rpt_battery_health AS
SELECT sd.sat_code,
       sd.day,
       sd.min_value AS min_v,
       sd.avg_value AS avg_v,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_low_battery_streak s
        WHERE s.sat_code = sd.sat_code AND date(s.started) = sd.day) AS low_streaks
FROM v_sensor_day sd
WHERE sd.type_code = 'batt_v';

-- Anomalies per satellite, sensor type and day.
CREATE VIEW rpt_anomaly_digest AS
SELECT sat_code,
       type_code,
       date(ts)   AS day,
       COUNT(*)   AS anomalies,
       MIN(ts)    AS first_at,
       MAX(value) AS highest,
       MIN(value) AS lowest
FROM v_anomaly
GROUP BY sat_code, type_code, date(ts);

-- How fresh each satellite's data is, against the newest reading in the fleet.
CREATE VIEW rpt_data_freshness AS
SELECT d.sat_code,
       MAX(l.last_ts) AS last_ts,
       (unixepoch((SELECT MAX(ts) FROM fact_reading)) - unixepoch(MAX(l.last_ts))) / 60
         AS minutes_behind
FROM v_latest_reading l
JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = l.sensor_key
GROUP BY d.sat_code;

-- The fleet's highest and lowest reading of each kind, and where and
-- when it happened. Ties go to the earlier reading, then the lower code.
CREATE VIEW rpt_sensor_extremes AS
SELECT type_code,
       extreme,
       sat_code,
       ts,
       value
FROM (
  SELECT d.type_code,
         'max' AS extreme,
         d.sat_code,
         f.ts,
         f.value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.type_code ORDER BY f.value DESC, f.ts, d.sat_code) AS pick
  FROM fact_reading f
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
  UNION ALL
  SELECT d.type_code,
         'min',
         d.sat_code,
         f.ts,
         f.value,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.type_code ORDER BY f.value, f.ts, d.sat_code)
  FROM fact_reading f
  JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
)
WHERE pick = 1;

-- The morning summary: one row per satellite that is not retired.
CREATE VIEW rpt_ops_summary AS
SELECT s.code AS sat_code,
       s.status,
       (SELECT ROUND(AVG(coverage_pct), 1) FROM rpt_fleet_daily f
        WHERE f.sat_code = s.code) AS coverage_pct,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_outage o WHERE o.sat_code = s.code) AS outages,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(o.gap_minutes), 0) FROM v_outage o
        WHERE o.sat_code = s.code) AS dark_minutes,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rpt_lost_passes p WHERE p.sat_code = s.code) AS lost_passes,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_low_battery_streak b WHERE b.sat_code = s.code) AS low_streaks,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_anomaly a WHERE a.sat_code = s.code) AS anomalies,
       (SELECT MAX(peak) FROM v_daily_peak_rank r
        WHERE r.sat_code = s.code AND r.type_code = 'cpu_t') AS max_cpu_t
FROM satellite s
WHERE s.status <> 'retired';

-- The summary as sentences, for the shift handover note.
CREATE VIEW rpt_handover AS
SELECT sat_code,
       printf('%s: %.1f%% coverage, %d outage(s) with %d minutes dark, %d lost pass(es), '
              || '%d low-battery streak(s), %d anomaly(ies)',
              sat_code, coverage_pct, outages, dark_minutes, lost_passes,
              low_streaks, anomalies) AS line
FROM rpt_ops_summary;

-- Each morning's summary is kept as JSON, so yesterday's report can still
-- be read after late data has changed today's numbers.
CREATE TABLE rpt_archive (
  as_of   TEXT NOT NULL,
  report  TEXT NOT NULL,
  body    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(body)),
  PRIMARY KEY (as_of, report)
);

INSERT INTO etl_run (batch_id)
SELECT DISTINCT batch_id
FROM landing_packet

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 12. Known-answer tests. Each expected value below was worked out by
--     hand from the development window's packets, not copied from the
--     pipeline's output. Each test_ view returns the rows where the
--     warehouse disagrees with the hand count: empty means pass.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE expect_count (
  test     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  item     TEXT    NOT NULL,
  expected INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test, item)
);

INSERT INTO expect_count (test, item, expected) VALUES
  ('sensors', 'ORB-1', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-2', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-3', 4),
  ('sensors', 'ORB-4', 4), ('sensors', 'ORB-5', 3), ('sensors', 'ORB-6', 4),
  ('passes',  'ORB-1', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-2', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-3', 6),
  ('passes',  'ORB-4', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-5', 6), ('passes',  'ORB-6', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_roster AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('sensors', 'passes')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'sensors' AS test, sat_code AS item, sensors AS actual FROM v_fleet_roster
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'passes', sat_code, passes FROM v_fleet_roster) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

  ('not_object', '1', 2), ('not_object', '2', 1), ('not_object', '3', 0);

CREATE VIEW test_staging AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('staged', 'not_object')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'staged' AS test, CAST(batch_id AS TEXT) AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT 'not_object', CAST(batch_id AS TEXT), SUM(NOT is_object)
                 FROM stg_reading GROUP BY batch_id) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_star AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.test, a.test) AS test,
       COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT test, item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test IN ('facts', 'dims')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT 'facts' AS test, d.sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM fact_reading f
                 JOIN dim_sensor d ON d.sensor_key = f.sensor_key
                 GROUP BY d.sat_code
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_satellite', COUNT(*) FROM dim_satellite
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_sensor',    COUNT(*) FROM dim_sensor
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_station',   COUNT(*) FROM dim_station
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'dims', 'dim_time',      COUNT(*) FROM dim_time) a
  ON a.test = e.test AND a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_rollup AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count
      WHERE test IN ('day', 'pass_fact')) e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT ds.sat_code || ' ' || a.day AS item, a.readings AS actual
                 FROM agg_satellite_day a
                 JOIN dim_satellite ds ON ds.sat_key = a.sat_key
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'planned', COUNT(*) FROM fact_pass
                 UNION ALL SELECT 'lost', SUM(readings_heard = 0) FROM fact_pass) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_gaps AS
SELECT 'sessions' AS test, COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS sat_code, a.actual AS at
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'sessions') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT sat_code AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
                 FROM v_contact_session GROUP BY sat_code) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual
UNION ALL
SELECT 'outage', sat_code, last_heard FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, last_heard, heard_again FROM expect_outage
  EXCEPT SELECT sat_code, last_heard, heard_again FROM v_outage)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'outage', sat_code, last_heard FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, last_heard, heard_again FROM v_outage
  EXCEPT SELECT sat_code, last_heard, heard_again FROM expect_outage)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'streak', sat_code, started FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, started, readings FROM expect_streak
  EXCEPT SELECT sat_code, started, readings FROM v_low_battery_streak)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'streak', sat_code, started FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, started, readings FROM v_low_battery_streak
  EXCEPT SELECT sat_code, started, readings FROM expect_streak);

-- The indexes the tuning work decided on, and no others.
CREATE VIEW test_indexes AS
SELECT COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS item,
       e.expected,
       a.actual
FROM (SELECT item, expected FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'index') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT name AS item, 1 AS actual
                 FROM sqlite_master
                 WHERE type = 'index' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_autoindex%') a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

CREATE VIEW test_history AS
SELECT 'status' AS test, sat_code, valid_from AS item FROM (
  SELECT sat_code, status, valid_from, valid_to FROM expect_status
  EXCEPT
  SELECT s.code, h.status, h.valid_from, h.valid_to
  FROM satellite_status_history h JOIN satellite s ON s.sat_id = h.sat_id
  WHERE s.code = 'ORB-2')
UNION ALL
SELECT 'status', sat_code, valid_from FROM (
  SELECT s.code AS sat_code, h.status, h.valid_from, h.valid_to
  FROM satellite_status_history h JOIN satellite s ON s.sat_id = h.sat_id
  WHERE s.code = 'ORB-2'
  EXCEPT
  SELECT sat_code, status, valid_from, valid_to FROM expect_status)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'audit', e.item, COALESCE(a.actual, 0)
FROM expect_count e
LEFT JOIN (SELECT table_name || ':' || action AS item, COUNT(*) AS actual
           FROM audit_log GROUP BY table_name, action) a ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.test = 'audit' AND e.expected IS NOT a.actual;

SELECT check_name,
       violations
FROM dq_summary
WHERE violations <> 0;

CREATE VIEW test_reports AS
SELECT 'lost pass ' || COALESCE(e.item, a.item) AS problem, NULL AS sat_code
FROM (SELECT item FROM expect_count WHERE test = 'lost_pass') e
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT CAST(pass_id AS TEXT) AS item FROM rpt_lost_passes) a
  ON a.item = e.item
WHERE e.item IS NULL OR a.item IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'missing or different', sat_code FROM (
  SELECT * FROM expect_ops_summary
  EXCEPT SELECT * FROM rpt_ops_summary)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'unexpected', sat_code FROM (
  SELECT * FROM rpt_ops_summary
  EXCEPT SELECT * FROM expect_ops_summary);

-- One line per test: how many rows disagree. All zeros is a green build.
CREATE VIEW test_summary AS
SELECT test, failures FROM (
            SELECT 'roster'      AS test, COUNT(*) AS failures FROM test_roster
  UNION ALL SELECT 'staging',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_staging
  UNION ALL SELECT 'quarantine',         COUNT(*)             FROM test_quarantine
  UNION ALL SELECT 'star',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_star
  UNION ALL SELECT 'lineage',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_lineage
  UNION ALL SELECT 'corrections',        COUNT(*)             FROM test_corrections
  UNION ALL SELECT 'rollup',             COUNT(*)             FROM test_rollup
  UNION ALL SELECT 'anomaly',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_anomaly
  UNION ALL SELECT 'gaps',               COUNT(*)             FROM test_gaps
  UNION ALL SELECT 'indexes',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_indexes
  UNION ALL SELECT 'history',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_history
  UNION ALL SELECT 'dq',                 COUNT(*)             FROM test_dq
  UNION ALL SELECT 'reports',            COUNT(*)             FROM test_reports
);

-- Archive this morning's summary, stamped with the newest batch's arrival.
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO rpt_archive (as_of, report, body)
SELECT (SELECT MAX(received_at) FROM landing_packet),
       'ops_summary',
       json_group_array(json_object('sat_code',     sat_code,
                                    'coverage_pct', coverage_pct,
                                    'outages',      outages,
                                    'dark_minutes', dark_minutes,
                                    'lost_passes',  lost_passes,
                                    'low_streaks',  low_streaks,
                                    'anomalies',    anomalies))
FROM (SELECT * FROM rpt_ops_summary ORDER BY sat_code);

+++ problem | A sensor leaves the fleet
--- task
When a sensor is removed from the operational `sensor` table, its row in `dim_sensor` must stay, because facts point at it, but `dq_dim_sensor_drift` then reports it as drift on every run. Change the design:

1. Add the column `is_current INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (is_current IN (0, 1))` as the last column of `dim_sensor`.
2. In the load step, right after the `dim_sensor` upsert, set `is_current` to 1 for every dimension row whose `sensor_id` is in `sensor`, and 0 for the others.
3. Make `dq_dim_sensor_drift` check only rows with `is_current = 1`.
4. Keep the data catalog complete.
--- starter
-- =====================================================================
--  ORBIT fleet telemetry warehouse
--
--  One script builds the whole database from an empty file that holds
--  only the landing zone (landing_packet). The layers, in the order the
--  data flows through them:
--
--    1. operational schema   the fleet, as the operations team keeps it
--    2. pipeline control     runs and steps, one trigger per step
--    3. staging              every landed packet, parsed, not trusted
--    4. quarantine           rejected packets, each with one reason
--    5. star schema          dimensions and the fact table
--    6. rollups              hourly and daily aggregates
--    7. trend reports        window functions over the facts
--    8. gaps and islands     outages, empty hours, low-battery streaks
--    9. data quality         checks that must return zero rows
--   10. report suite         what operations reads every morning
--
--  Conventions: times are UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; every step can
--  be rerun for the same batch without changing the result.
-- =====================================================================

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Operational schema: the fleet as the operations team keeps it.
--    Normalised: each fact about the fleet is stored exactly once, and
--    the constraints refuse any row that could not be true.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE satellite (
  sat_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (code GLOB 'ORB-[0-9]*'),
  name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
  launched_on  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (launched_on IS date(launched_on)),
  status       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                       CHECK (status IN ('active', 'safe_mode', 'retired')),
  status_since TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status_since >= launched_on)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor_type (
  type_code  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CHECK (type_code = lower(type_code)),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,
  unit       TEXT NOT NULL,
  min_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  max_valid  REAL NOT NULL,
  CHECK (min_valid < max_valid)
);

CREATE TABLE sensor (
  sensor_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  type_code  TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES sensor_type (type_code),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, type_code)
);

CREATE TABLE ground_station (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (length(code) = 3 AND code = upper(code)),
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  latitude   REAL NOT NULL CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90),
  longitude  REAL NOT NULL CHECK (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180)
);

-- A planned contact: the satellite is above the station's horizon from
-- aos (acquisition of signal) until los (loss of signal).
CREATE TABLE contact_pass (
  pass_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellite (sat_id),
  station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_station (station_id),
  aos        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (aos IS datetime(aos, '+0 seconds')),
  los        TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (los IS datetime(los, '+0 seconds')),
  CHECK (los > aos),
  UNIQUE (sat_id, aos)
);
